f8f4107586036d36: SUNGAI SIPUT: Joe Zamberi, 23, was walking ahead of his father when he heard a scream before turning around to witness a tiger attacking his father in Kampung Takung, Pos Perwor, here yesterday.
Joe said he and his father, Zamberi Angah, had gone to the Korbu Forest Reserve around 8am to collect rattan before deciding to return home at 3pm.
"I heard my father scream. I turned around and screamed too. Then it (the tiger) dragged my father away.
"I was scared, so I ran and immediately called the villagers," he said when met today.
Joe, who was still shaken by the incident, said he found it difficult to describe what had happened.
Asked about his relationship with his father and his late father's final message, Joe became emotional and said they were close before being unable to continue speaking.
Zamberi, 42, was found dead at 6.58pm in a bamboo grove near a logging road, about 200 metres from where the attack occurred.
Tiger paw prints and other clues were found at the location where the body was discovered.
The Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) received a report about the incident about 4.30pm before a search operation began at 6.30pm.
The search operation also involved police from the Lintang police station, members of the Malaysian Volunteers Corps (Rela), and about 30 villagers and logging workers.
10c1aa275e8401d6: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — The Malaysian Palm Oil Council (MPOC) foresees Malaysia’s palm oil exports remaining stable at around 16 million tonnes in 2027, with the country expected to play an increasingly important role in supplying palm oil to global consumers.

Citing independent global market analyses and forecasts by Oil World, MPOC said Indonesia’s palm oil production is forecast to decline by 1.9 million tonnes in 2027, while Malaysia’s production is forecast to fall by 0.7 million tonnes.
“Indonesia’s exports are also projected to decline by almost three million tonnes in 2027, reflecting firmer domestic demand from biodiesel blending and a weaker production outlook.

“As a result, Malaysia is expected to become an increasingly important source of palm oil for global consumers, while the country’s current high stock level is likely to be temporary,” it said in a statement today.

MPOC noted that Malaysia’s palm oil production rose marginally by 1.4 per cent month-on-month to 1.81 million tonnes in August 2026, supported by higher fresh fruit bunch collection and an improvement in the oil extraction rate from July.

Nonetheless, output remained below the level recorded a year earlier, marking the sixth consecutive month of year-on-year decline since March 2026, while cumulative palm oil exports from January to August 2026 rose by 806,000 tonnes to 10.4 million tonnes.
However, exports fell 7.5 per cent month-on-month in August to 1.29 million tonnes, weighed by weaker shipments to South Asia and the Middle East.
Despite the monthly decline, MPOC said full-year exports are projected to reach 16.0 million tonnes, 5.2 per cent higher than the volume recorded in 2025.
The combination of higher production and weaker exports lifted palm oil stocks to 2.82 million tonnes in August.

Looking ahead, it said crude palm oil prices are expected to remain firm above RM4,700 per tonne in October and likely throughout the rest of the year, underpinned by weather uncertainty and favourable energy markets.
“The main downside risks are an easing in energy prices and further stock accumulation, as palm oil production typically reaches its seasonal peak in September or October,” it added. — Bernama
8759034929a2c6a3: NAGOYA, Sept 22 — Malaysia booked their place in the men’s team regu sepak takraw semi-finals of the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games as Group B winners after a 3-0 victory over India at Nagoya City Mizuho Arena here today.
Malaysia topped the group with three wins and will face the Group A runners-up, either South Korea or Indonesia, in the semi-finals on Thursday.

The national team took the lead through Muhammad Zulkifli Abd Razak, Muhammad Afifuddin Mohd Razali and Aidil Aiman Azwawi, who were made to work hard before defeating India’s first trio of Malemnganba Singh Sorokhaibam, Arun and Akash Yumnam 2-1 (15-13, 11-15, 15-6).
Malaysia’s main trio of Mohammad Syahir Mohd Rosdi, Mohamad Azlan Alias and Farhan Adam then secured the second point with a 2-0 (15-9, 15-12) win.
The third trio of Muhammad Zarif Marican, Amirul Zazwan Amir and Muhammad Hafizul Hayazi Adnan completed the clean sweep with a 2-0 (15-11, 15-5) victory over India’s final trio.
Malaysia had earlier opened their campaign with a 3-0 win over hosts Japan before producing an identical result against the Philippines.
The national team are now chasing their first gold in the team regu event since their last victory at the Beijing 1990 Asian Games, 36 years ago.
National head coach Ahmad Jais Baharun said the players needed to sharpen several aspects of their game, particularly concentration, shot variation and first-ball touches, ahead of the semi-finals.

“Overall, we are satisfied with the players’ performance. However, there are elements we need to emphasise going into the semi-finals so that we do not become complacent or lose focus in such an important match.
“We need to improve our concentration and shot variation, while our first ball was somewhat loose in the second set of the main regu. Those are among the things we identified,” he said. — Bernama

f9fdfb6fee703169: BEIJING: Chinese street dancer Wu Yufei has spent most of his 13-year career performing solo, but this year, he found some new partners – a crew of robots with sleek moves.
The 27-year-old Sichuan native, together with his fellow robot performers, has made it to the final of "America's Got Talent" (AGT), a stage he had been hoping to reach for years.
A longstanding science-fiction fan, Wu told AFP from Pasadena, California, that dancing with robots in the group Homies gave him a "very magical feeling".
After months of training with them, his robot dancers now feel like more than just "cold, lifeless machines", he said.
"It almost feels as if there's a kind of team spirit there," Wu told AFP, as he and the dance crew of humanoids – made by Chinese robotics group Unitree – prepared for the AGT final this week.

Robot dancing has become a huge craze in China after Unitree robots performed in a breakout performance at China's annual Spring Festival gala performance, the country's most-watched television extravaganza.
Businesses and event planners across the country have since rushed to hire robots to perform and attract visitors.
Training robots to dance involves capturing intricate human movements, running computer simulations, and then transferring results to the robots, said industry insiders.
For Fang Zhenghua, the art director behind Wu and Unitree's AGT performances, training a robot to dance resembles "creating a soul".
"The impact of AI on dance performances, or the impact of robots on dancing – I was quite against it all at the beginning," he told AFP from Shanghai.
But over time, working with the skilled engineers – who he describes as the "mothers" of the robots – changed his perspective.
SCRIPTED CHOREOGRAPHY
Training robots requires input from human dancers and relies heavily on engineers to troubleshoot problems, particularly in real-time during performances.
"It takes a lot of fine-tuning," Liu Zhiquan, commercialisation lead at robotics motion-capture firm BridgeDP, told AFP.
A 30-second dance routine could take days, sometimes weeks, to perfect, he added, and performers need to be willing to compromise.
"If the dancers are not tech-savvy, there will be a lot of re-takes," he said.
Wegers Wei, from Shanghai-based dance studio Limit Crew, said that when he designs routines for robots, he avoids movements that he knows will be difficult for them.

"If we find that some routines don't look good for robots or if they look like the robots are making mistakes, we would change them," said Wei, whose robots won first and second places for street dance at this year's World Humanoid Robot Games.
Robots are good at rotating moves, or what street dancers call power moves, Wei said, as it is "just a matter of adjusting the motor power and the torque of the arms".
However, routines that require body flexibility are extremely difficult for robots, he said.
Another blind spot is musicality.
Robot dancing is mostly scripted playback.
Unlike humans, the machines cannot improvise or "make on-the-spot adjustments" if the music changes suddenly, Wu Yufei added.
BEYOND ENTERTAINMENT
While the general public in China mostly sees robot dancing as entertainment, industry insiders see it as a chance to show off robotic designs, capabilities and reliability.
"That's why everyone is keen to perform these kinds of high-skill dances," said Guo Renjie, founder and CEO of robotics engineering company Zeroth.
A recent Morgan Stanley report forecast that China's humanoid robotics market could reach US$2 billion in value this year.
Accounting for more than 97 per cent of humanoid robot shipments in the first half of 2026 globally, the Chinese industry also faces increasing scrutiny from investors and policymakers.
Many companies are struggling to find commercially viable uses for their humanoids beyond entertainment.
Executives at humanoid robotics companies have publicly acknowledged that the industry is still years away from its own "ChatGPT moment" – the point at which robots become useful to ordinary people.
"I think everyone should give this industry time to reach its full potential," said Zeroth's Guo.
Unitree made a blistering debut on the Shanghai stock market in August, surging 629 per cent through the first day's trading.
Its market capitalisation has since fallen by around half from its peak.
Back at the AGT filming studio in Pasadena, Wu pointed to another robot benefit – how quickly his robot crew could learn routines.
"Their knowledge can be replicated extremely quickly," he said.
"Not only does a single robot learn quickly, but they can all learn the same things at the same time, which is quite terrifying."

5d46fe32b73c953e: NEW YORK: The US on Monday reiterated its commitment to the defence of key Asian allies Japan and South Korea, and the three nations expressed support for Taiwan ahead of a summit this week between US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

Analysts say the US allies are anxious that Trump may offer concessions to Xi including over Taiwan and trade in return for an economic win with Beijing when he hosts Xi at the White House in Washington on Thursday.

Officials say both Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and South Korean President Lee Jae Myung are keen to see the US president during the UN General Assembly in New York, where all three are scheduled to speak on Tuesday.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with his South Korean counterpart Cho Hyun and Japan's Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi in New York on Monday.

They issued a joint statement vowing, in apparent reference to China, to stand firm "against economic coercion and non-market policies and practices" and "arbitrary export restrictions that disrupt supply chains."
They also welcomed the launch of a new trilateral consultation mechanism on economic security, part of broader efforts to strengthen supply chains and cooperation on critical technologies.

The statement said the US "reiterated its ironclad commitments to the defence of Japan and the ROK, backed by America's unmatched military strength, including its nuclear capabilities, and reaffirmed its extended deterrence commitments to Japan and the ROK," using the initials for the Republic of Korea, South Korea's official name.
The statement said the ministers emphasised their commitment to robust security cooperation and the importance of maintaining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait.
It also "expressed support for Taiwan's meaningful participation in appropriate international organisations."

In a statement, its foreign ministry said the renewed joint public support for maintaining peace and stability shows that security in the strait has become a "strong consensus of the international community."
Referring to North Korea, the ministers "reaffirmed their resolute commitment to the complete denuclearisation of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea" and called on it to resume dialogue.

In addition to concerns about Taiwan, a democratically governed island China claims as its own, analysts said allies will be scrutinising any trade announcements from the Trump-Xi summit for their impact on competitiveness relative to China.
Even a modest reduction in trade barriers for Beijing could erode their positions.

Takaichi angered Beijing last year by saying Tokyo could be drawn into a conflict over Taiwan, and Seoul and Washington have been negotiating details of South Korea's US$350 billion investment package in the US under a trade deal struck by the allies last year.

On Monday, a South Korean opposition lawmaker called for parliamentary scrutiny of the investment package, warning that negotiations over energy projects could leave South Korea carrying disproportionate financial risks.
d5fdcaf404ab49b9: SUBANG JAYA: They posed as tourists who came to enjoy the beauty of this country.

However, the ruse by several foreign women in their early 20s was exposed when they were detained while they were believed to be carrying out illegal dental treatment at a luxury clinic in Subang Jaya yesterday.
The woman claimed she was only acting as a health consultant when she was detained for questioning in a treatment room at the premises.

The woman was among four foreign nationals detained during a raid by a team of dental enforcement officers from the Dental Health Division, Selangor State Health Department and the Oral Health Programme of the Health Ministry, together with five Immigration Department officers yesterday.

The raid was carried out after intelligence found that the clinic, believed to be popular among high-income groups, was offering suspicious dental services and was suspected of being operated by foreign nationals who were not qualified to practise dentistry.
A Health Ministry spokesman said checks found that the premises was registered and authorised to operate as a private dental clinic.
He said there was also a qualified local dentist at the clinic who provided treatment in a separate room.
However, intelligence found that several foreign nationals were present and offering suspicious treatment at the same premises.
They claimed to have professional qualifications to carry out dental treatment.

Among them were two foreign women in their 20s. During questioning, one of them claimed she was only acting as a health consultant, offering advice and treatment plans to customers interested in implant or denture procedures.
He said an inspection of the room also found X-ray images showing a patient's teeth displayed on a computer screen.
The woman, who claimed to have medical qualifications from her home country, failed to provide a reasonable explanation when questioned by Health Ministry investigating officers.
She also claimed to be in Malaysia as a foreign tourist and was unable to provide a convincing answer about her connection to the clinic.

Health Ministry enforcement officers also believed another foreign man, who was suspected of carrying out dental treatment without authorisation, had fled through the back door of the premises after becoming aware of the raid.
The claim was supported by the discovery of a personal bag believed to belong to the man, which had been left behind in the treatment room.
Further inspection also found various medicines and dental equipment from overseas, whose use and approval status were questionable.
Dental equipment and materials believed to have been used for implant procedures were also found stored in a storeroom at the premises.
The spokesman said the foreign nationals failed to produce a Certificate of Registration with the Malaysian Dental Council and an Annual Practising Certificate during the inspection.
He said an investigation would be conducted under the provisions of the Dental Act 2018 (Act 804).
The Health Ministry said individuals practising dentistry without registration could face action under Section 62(1) of the Dental Act 2018 and, if convicted, be punished under Section 62(3).
The individuals are also suspected of violating Section 63(1)(d) of the Dental Act 2018 and, if convicted, can be punished under Section 63(2) of the same Act, it said.
The Health Ministry had previously explained that only qualified, competent, professional and registered dental practitioners are allowed to provide dental services in Malaysia.
Practising dentists must also have a valid Annual Practising Certificate, which must be renewed annually.
The case is being investigated and further action will be taken against those involved in accordance with the relevant laws.

8b66179a77664601: KUALA LUMPUR: Senior pair Pearly Tan-M. Thinaah won the battle, but Malaysia lost the war against South Korea, suffering an agonising quarter-final exit in the women's team event in Ichinomiya City on Tuesday.

Despite world No. 5 Pearly-Thinaah's valiant effort in toppling world No. 2 Baek Ha Na-Lee So Hee 22-20, 21-17 in a 61-minute first doubles match, An Se Young-led South Korea clinched a 3-1 victory to reach the semi-finals.
World No. 1 Se Young was in her element in the first singles, outplaying Malaysia's world No. 28 K. Letshanaa 21-12, 21-8 in 36 minutes to give the Koreans the expected start.
However, Pearly-Thinaah produced arguably their best performance of the year when they stunned the world champions Ha Na-So Hee in straight games to keep Malaysia's hopes alive.
In the second singles, world No. 37 Wong Ling Ching was unable to contain a more composed world No. 12 Kim Ga Eun and was beaten 21-12, 21-18 as Malaysia fell 2-1 behind.

Second doubles pair Cheng Su Yin-Low Zi Yu battled valiantly before suffering a narrow 18-21, 21-11, 24-22 defeat to Jeong Na Eun-Kim Hye Jeong in a clash between scratch pairs, ending Malaysia's campaign in the last eight.
The defeat also means Malaysia's 64-year drought for a medal in the women's team event continues as their last medal effort was at the 1962 Jakarta Games, where they clinched silver.

dd3434aa0444316a: KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL) is seeking the public's assistance in tracking down the family members or acquaintances of a patient who has been receiving treatment at the hospital since Aug 17.

HKL said the patient, who goes by the name 'Thambirajan', was admitted to the Emergency and Trauma Department after suffering a stroke, but was not carrying any identification documents and was unable to provide further information about himself.
"An investigation by the HKL Medical Social Work Department also found that the patient was unable to provide his full name and identification card number," HKL said in a statement.

The HKL Medical Social Work Department also referred the patient to the National Registration Department (NRD) to obtain further information on his identity, but checks found that the patient's details did not match any NRD records.

65d3ed4d0bcedf03: AYER KEROH: Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh is scheduled to hold a special press conference this afternoon.

1ed8d377bc2b1a3f: NEW YORK: The United Kingdom has signed on to an initiative urging UN Security Council permanent members to withhold their vetoes on matters concerning mass atrocities, such as genocide, countries leading the push said Monday.

The initiative, first proposed by Mexico and France in 2015, now has a total of 128 countries behind it, French foreign minister Jean-Noel Barrot and Mexican counterpart Roberto Velasco said in a joint statement.
It is now just one country shy of reaching a two-thirds threshold of UN member states.
The Security Council has been paralysed on many issues in recent years amid deep divisions between the five veto-wielding permanent members: France, UK, Russia, China, and the United States.

"By supporting this political declaration, states are demonstrating their commitment to ensuring that the Security Council can fully exercise its primary responsibility for maintaining international peace and security," said Barrot and Velasco.
In May, a diplomatic source told AFP that France was hoping to reach the two-thirds majority before this year's UN General Assembly, which kicks off this week.
Even if adopted with a two-thirds majority, the resolution would be non-binding.
Officials nonetheless hope to make it more politically difficult for a permanent member to use its veto in cases of such dire emergencies.
8721eb89d116b644: KUALA LUMPUR: The Indian High Commission in Kuala Lumpur has warned Indian nationals against using Malaysia's 30-day visa-free facility to seek employment.
This follows a noticeable increase in arrivals of people misled by bogus job offers.

In an advisory posted on its official X account, the high commission said the visa-free facility, which allows Indian passport holders to stay in Malaysia for up to 30 days, is strictly for tourism and social visits, and using it to seek employment constitutes a clear violation of immigration rules.
"There is a noticeable increase in Indian nationals arriving in Malaysia using the 30-day visa-free facility, to seek employment.

"The High Commission of India, Kuala Lumpur alerts Indian nationals travelling to Malaysia on tourist visas against taking up employment. Many Indian nationals are misled by unscrupulous agents with false job promises, leading to overstay, illegal status, exploitation, detention, and legal action," it said.
The high commission reiterated that Indian nationals should not travel to Malaysia for employment without a valid work permit or visa with reference (VDR).

"Genuine tourists must carry valid and verifiable documentation such as confirmed return ticket, hotel booking, online submission of the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) three days before the arrival date, and a passport with minimum 6-month validity, to avoid any immigration-related issues on arrival in Malaysia," the high commission said.
861c03147ed99568: KOTA BARU: Kelantan recorded losses of RM33.47 million in commercial crime from January to August this year, an increase of RM5.97 million compared with RM27.50 million reported during the same period last year.
Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the number of commercial crime cases also rose from 1,100 to 1,921, an increase of 821 cases.
He said one of the most significant increases was in e-commerce scams, which rose from 260 to 657 cases, while other cybercrimes also increased from 287 to 444 cases.

"This trend shows that crime is increasingly changing in line with technological developments. Therefore, our actions must also change rapidly, particularly in prevention and public awareness," he said in his speech at the monthly assembly at the Kelantan police headquarters today.
However, Yusoff said the overall crime index for the Kelantan contingent from January to August this year fell three per cent to 1,213 cases compared with 1,251 cases during the same period in 2025.
He said violent crime also declined 11 per cent from 310 to 276 cases, while property crime fell from 941 to 937 cases.
On the drug threat, he said narcotics cases decreased 13 per cent from 18,427 to 16,044 during the period, while arrests fell 10 per cent from 19,469 to 17,579.
He said the value of drugs seized also declined 31.49 per cent from RM25.47 million to RM17.45 million, as a result of more systematic and focused efforts to combat the threat.
In terms of prevention, Yusoff said the state police continued to implement various approaches, including patrols, Amanita, community policing programmes and networks with relevant agencies.

He said community participation through the Volunteer Smartphone Patrol (VSP) also needed to be further strengthened, with 150,019 people having registered as VSP members in the Kelantan contingent as of Aug 31.

He said efforts to engage with young people should also take into account the influence of screens, social media and the digital world, which increasingly shape their lives, while maintaining face-to-face interaction to build public trust.
Yusoff said these ongoing efforts were important to ensure that public safety was always safeguarded, in line with the police's responsibility to maintain peace in the state.
5d34eb543fb12ab7: KUALA TERENGGANU, Sept 22 — The Department of Fisheries Malaysia (DOF), through the Rantau Abang Turtle and Marine Ecosystem Centre (TCIC), recorded three leatherback turtle (Dermochelys coriacea) landings along the Terengganu coast this month, involving 195 eggs that were transferred to a controlled incubation site for protection.
Director-General of Fisheries Datuk Adnan Hussain said the records provide important data to monitor leatherback turtle landings, protect the eggs and improve their survival chances.
The first nesting was recorded at Pasir Putih Beach, Marang, on Sept 1, involving 44 eggs, followed by 81 eggs at Rantau Abang Beach on Sept 13 and 70 eggs at Kuala Abang Beach today.
He said conservation officers successfully located and measured the nesting mother turtle during the third landing at Kuala Abang Beach at about 2am today.
The turtle measured 215 centimetres in carapace length and 115 centimetres in width.
Staff transferred all 70 eggs to the TCIC incubation site at about 6am and reburied them at a depth of 80 to 100 centimetres to replicate natural nesting conditions.
“The incubation period is expected to last between 55 and 70 days, depending on sand temperature, with TCIC conducting periodic monitoring of the nest conditions,” he said in a statement today.

Adnan said sustained conservation efforts, including scientific monitoring, nest management, enforcement and public awareness, as well as cooperation from local communities and fishermen, were crucial to protecting the species.
He urged the public not to disturb or touch sea turtles coming ashore but to immediately report sightings to the DOF for appropriate action.
The DOF also reminded the public that sea turtles and their eggs are protected under relevant laws.

Under the Terengganu Turtle Enactment 1951 (Amendment 2021), offences involving the possession or sale of eggs, or disturbance of sea turtles, carry fines of between RM50,000 and RM250,000 and imprisonment of up to one year, or both, upon conviction.
The department also called on fishing communities, local residents and the public to report any sea turtle landings or sightings to facilitate timely protection and conservation measures. — Bernama
a7aec9b39de6f0fd: PARIT BUNTAR: Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah today officially opened the RM173.3 million Parit Buntar Hospital, which is expected to strengthen healthcare services for thousands of residents in Kerian and surrounding areas.
Also present were Raja Permaisuri Perak Tuanku Zara Salim and Raja Di-Hilir Perak Raja Iskandar Dzulkarnain Sultan Idris.

Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the government remained committed to strengthening healthcare facilities to ensure equitable access to quality medical services, in line with the Health White Paper.

He said Perak currently had one psychiatric institution, 14 hospitals, 89 health clinics, 78 dental clinics, 10 maternal and child health clinics, 188 rural clinics and 16 community clinics serving its population.
Dzulkefly said the development of the 5.594ha Parit Buntar Hospital was particularly significant for Kerian, which has nearly 170,000 residents and shares borders with Penang and Kedah.
"The new hospital has emerged as an important referral healthcare facility in the northern region, complementing the state's existing healthcare network," he said in his speech.
Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and Perak Health Department director Datuk Dr Feisul Idzwan Mustapha attended the ceremony

Construction of the hospital began in January 2018 and was fully completed on July 23 last year, despite challenges including work to stabilise the paddy field soil structure and disruptions caused by the Covid-19 pandemic.
The hospital began operations on Sept 3 last year.
He said the hospital comprised six blocks with 76 beds, including male, female, paediatric and maternity wards, as well as a High Dependency Unit.

Its maternity suite has six delivery rooms and a three-bed observation bay, while its clinical capabilities are supported by a Respiratory and Haemodynamic Unit, Pregnancy Assessment Centre and two operating theatres.
He said one of the operating theatres had been operational since April 3 this year.

"The facility also provides comprehensive clinical support services, including specialist clinics, haemodialysis, imaging and diagnostics, pathology and transfusion services, as well as pharmacy services," he said.
He added that specialists in internal medicine and emergency medicine had also been stationed at the hospital to ensure patients received appropriate specialist care.
However, Dzulkefly said the availability of modern healthcare facilities alone would not be enough to build a healthy society.
He urged the public to take greater responsibility for their own health and that of their families, stressing that healthcare should begin at home.
"I believe that healthy people are the state's most important asset, because only through physical and mental well-being can the nation and its people be developed and prosper," he said.
de6c9949386720a1: GEORGE TOWN: A leatherback turtle's return to Terengganu three times this month is a positive development for the species' conservation, says the Fisheries Department.

The turtle, believed to be the same individual, first landed at Rantau Abang and laid 44 eggs before returning to the same area and laying another 81.
It came ashore again last night at Kuala Abang and laid 70 eggs, bringing the total to 195 eggs across three nesting attempts.
Adnan said the turtle's repeated landings were consistent with the nesting behaviour of the species, which can return to shore several times during a nesting season.
He urged the public not to disturb the turtle and to give Fisheries Department personnel sufficient space to protect and manage the eggs.
"We hope these eggs will hatch successfully and contribute meaningfully to turtle conservation efforts in the country."
Adnan said no disturbances had been reported during the turtle's three landings, describing the public's response and cooperation as encouraging.
He said the leatherback, the world's largest turtle species, was estimated to measure about 2.15m in length.
"This is an exceptionally large turtle. Usually, the leatherback turtles we encounter are just over one metre long, so a turtle measuring more than two metres is certainly significant," he added.
Adnan said the eggs would be protected and managed by the Fisheries Department, with efforts focused on allowing them to hatch under natural conditions.
He said the department's collaboration with Aquawalk Sdn Bhd, Angsana Teluk Bahang and Universiti Malaysia Terengganu (UMT) was aimed at strengthening marine turtle conservation and public education.
The partnership also saw the establishment of a Marine Education Centre to increase awareness of endangered marine species and promote wider participation in conservation efforts.

Adnan said collaboration involving government agencies, the corporate sector, the hospitality industry and universities would help strengthen conservation efforts, particularly in Penang and other key marine habitats.

b304fbe0c3e041f2: GEORGE TOWN: Piranha and pacu can adapt to Malaysia's tropical freshwater environment, raising concerns about their potential impact if released into local waters.

Fisheries Department director-general Datuk Adnan Hussain said both species were foreign fish prohibited from being released into public waters, with enforcement continuing against their illegal possession and sale.
He said piranha could theoretically survive and reproduce in Malaysian waters as its natural habitat in the Amazon had a tropical climate similar to Malaysia's.
"If we look at the original ecosystem of piranha in the Amazon River, Brazil, it has an equatorial climate like ours.

"So, generally, it could reproduce in our ecosystem because the weather is similar to its natural habitat," he told reporters after launching the Marine Education Centre at Angsana Teluk Bahang here today.
Adnan said this made it important for the department to establish whether a fish reportedly caught at Klau Dam recently was a piranha or pacu.

He said preliminary analysis of video footage showed the fish's morphology appeared closer to that of a piranha, but the department could not confirm its identity as the physical specimen had been discarded.
"We can only conclude that it resembles the piranha genus. However, we cannot confirm the species because we only have video footage and no physical specimen," he said.
Adnan said the department had contacted inland fishermen operating around Klau Dam and asked them to preserve and surrender any suspected piranha or pacu caught in the area.
He said a physical specimen would allow the department to examine its morphology, scales and teeth before confirming its genus and species.
Adnan said the department was also exploring DNA and environmental DNA (eDNA) analysis with Aquaria KLCC, which has live piranha specimens and DNA references.
"We will work with Aquaria to identify the fish through DNA and eDNA analysis and determine its genus and species," he said.
Adnan said the department had yet to establish whether a piranha population existed at Klau Dam, stressing that the available evidence remained inconclusive.

"I cannot confirm it because we only have one video, and even the location was based on a claim that it was at Klau Dam. We do not have concrete evidence at this time. We are still monitoring the situation," he said.
He said the department had also received reports from other inland fishermen who claimed to have encountered similar fish, but the specimens had been discarded, preventing verification.
Adnan said there had been no reports of sudden fish deaths or anglers being attacked by suspected piranha following the reported sighting.
He also warned that prohibited ornamental fish continued to be offered for sale online, prompting the department to engage platform operators on the requirements governing foreign fish species.
He said even permitted foreign live fish brought into Malaysia must be accompanied by a health certificate to ensure they were free from diseases that could threaten the country's aquatic ecosystem.
"We will continue inspections at ornamental fish premises nationwide and take action where necessary to ensure our ecosystem remains protected from invasive fish species," he said.
Adnan said those found possessing prohibited fish without approval could face a fine of up to RM100,000 under the Fisheries Act 1985.

He added that holders of permits for foreign ornamental fish must maintain traceability and report the status of their fish to the department, including when they die, to prevent them from being released into public waters.

064b6f929b85e934: GEORGE TOWN: A construction company owner was charged with submitting false information to the Social Security Organisation (Socso) in a 2022 targeted wage subsidy claim.

fbcf3cd523b527da: LETTERS: The threat of transboundary haze could put pressure on the targets of Visit Malaysia 2026 (VM2026).
AN empirical study of previous crises by the Economy and Environment Programme for Southeast Asia (EEPSEA) found that air pollution could reduce tourist arrivals by up to eight per cent.
This results in direct losses to the sector of more than RM300 million and contributes to losses to the national gross domestic product (GDP) of up to RM1.5 billion.
In light of this, more creative action is needed. One approach worth considering is dynamically changing destinations, or dynamic rerouting.

When a destination has air quality conditions less suitable for outdoor activities, tourists can be offered the option to change part of their itinerary to another more suitable area, based on current air quality information and advice from the authorities.

For example, if an area on the west coast of Peninsular Malaysia is affected, tourists could be offered alternative experiences in other destinations with better air quality, subject to prevailing conditions.
For international tourists, this approach matters because they have already incurred costs for flights, accommodation, and travel expenses.
For domestic tourists, it could prevent an entire holiday from being cancelled simply because one location is no longer suitable to visit.
And when a risk keeps returning, having an alternative plan is no longer simply an option. It becomes part of the preparation.
Thus, the industry needs to have alternative plans in place before disruptions occur.
Malaysia has a diverse range of cultural, culinary and heritage products that can be utilised to reduce reliance on outdoor activities.

These include visits to museums, galleries, science centres, indoor theme parks, shopping centres, cultural performances, craft workshops and cooking classes, which can be incorporated into alternative packages.
During a crisis, communication is just as important as the product itself.
Relevant agencies need to keep tourists updated on which areas are affected, which activities to avoid, and what options are available.
If the information only states that Malaysia is experiencing haze, tourists may assume that the entire country is affected in the same way. This is where technology and data can help.

The development of artificial intelligence and machine learning in the tourism industry enables companies to analyse customer data, identify demand patterns, manage pricing and inventory, and provide more personalised travel recommendations.
In the context of haze, a data-driven approach could help the industry identify demand shifts and offer alternatives based on conditions at different destinations.

In the face of haze, the tourism sector's sustainability depends not only on its ability to attract tourists, but also on its ability to provide meaningful experiences and economic value even when disruptions occur.
AKMAL ADANAN, Senior Lecturer, Faculty of Hotel and Tourism Management, UiTM, Melaka

52b9949c68661f29: BEIJING: Alibaba Group plans to train a new artificial intelligence model with between 5.0 trillion and 10 trillion parameters, chief executive Eddie Wu said on Tuesday, as the Chinese technology giant outlined a sweeping strategy encompassing artificial intelligence (AI) models, chips and data centres.

Speaking at Alibaba Cloud's annual Apsara Conference in Hangzhou, Wu said the company's Qwen team was continuing research into model architecture and data optimisation, with the goal of completing "more complex, longer-horizon tasks" and advancing toward artificial superintelligence, or ASI.

In a separate statement, Alibaba said its next-generation model, Qwen 4, was currently in training, adding that the upcoming Qwen 4.5 and Qwen 5 series were projected to scale up to 5.0 trillion to 10 trillion parameters.
Parameters are the variables a model learns during training and are a rough gauge of its size.
Alibaba's current flagship model, Qwen 3.8 Max, has 2.4 trillion parameters, meaning the planned model would be roughly two to four times larger.
Wu said Alibaba's proprietary M890 AI supernode already handles inference for models above 2 trillion parameters, a capability he said only "a handful of companies globally" possess.

The Qwen team has made "meaningful progress" on recursive self-improvement, in which models identify their own limitations, design experiments and synthesise data to drive a cycle of self-evolution, he said.
Alibaba also introduced the Zhenwu V900, a next-generation AI chip from its T-Head semiconductor unit, which Wu called the most powerful AI chip in China.
It delivers three times the performance of its predecessor, the M890, and a single cluster built on it can support up to 500,000 cards for frontier model training and inference, he said.
The chip is scheduled for mass production and commercial release in the first quarter of 2027, the company said in the statement. The M890 was released in May.
The company expects "significant growth" in annual AI chip shipments, Wu said.
The launch comes as Chinese firms race to build domestic alternatives to Nvidia's processors amid US export restrictions.
Wu set a target for Alibaba Cloud's global data centre capacity to surpass 20 gigawatts by 2032.

He said customer demand for AI remained "exceptionally robust" and was accelerating Alibaba Cloud's revenue growth but acknowledged that global shortages across the AI data centre supply chain were limiting how fast the company could expand.
"The industry's mid-to-long-term demand far outpaces our supply capabilities," he said, adding that Alibaba Cloud would begin bringing its AI supernodes online at commercial scale this quarter.

Wu framed the moment as the dawn of an era of "machine intelligence" comparable to the Industrial Revolution, predicting machines would eventually produce more than 1,000 times the "thinking" of all humanity, up from less than 3.0 per cent today.
He likened AI coding to the light bulb of the electrical age – an early application rather than the breakthrough product.
"The truly groundbreaking products of the machine intelligence era have not yet arrived," he said.
da3096ba66398f3b: KUALA LUMPUR: U Mobile and ZTE Corporation have completed a proof-of-concept (POC) of a portable, fully off-grid 5G network site powered entirely by 100 per cent green energy, demonstrating a faster and more sustainable approach to extending connectivity to remote and underserved communities.

The network provider said in a statement today that the site is powered entirely by solar energy and connected directly to U Mobile's core network via satellite backhaul; the solution can operate independently of both the national electricity grid and terrestrial transmission infrastructure such as fibre.
It said this enables deployment in locations where conventional network infrastructure may be difficult or time-consuming to build.

"The POC demonstrated that the site can be installed and fully activated within just three days, compared with nearly a year for conventional tower deployments in challenging rural locations," it added.

U Mobile said the POC was piloted at SK Mentu, a primary school in Sebuyau, Sarawak, and Balai Kebudayaan Iburu, a community hall in Sipitang, Sabah, whereby at each location, a lightweight 12-metre pole structure was installed in place of a conventional telecommunications tower.

Supported by high-efficiency solar panels and a battery backup system capable of operating for up to 52 hours without sunlight, depending on configuration, the sites supported both 4G and 5G services and achieved peak download speeds of up to 134 megabits per second during live testing, it said.

U Mobile chief technology officer Woon Ooi Yuen said the POC demonstrated how a 100 per cent green-energy, off-grid site could be deployed rapidly while still delivering reliable 4G and 5G connectivity.
"As Malaysia's newest 5G network provider, we have the opportunity to explore more agile ways of expanding our network, particularly in areas where conventional deployment can be challenging.

"Together with technology partners such as ZTE, we will continue to explore practical innovations that can accelerate the expansion of our ULTRA5G network, help close the digital divide and extend the benefits of connectivity to more Malaysians," he said.

Meanwhile, ZTE Malaysia chief marketing officer Tey Khang Lian said the collaboration combined solar power, battery storage and satellite backhaul in a portable rural network solution that addressed key infrastructure challenges in remote areas.
"This rural pilot POC reflects our shared commitment to making 4G and 5G connectivity more accessible and supporting Malaysia's digital inclusion aspirations," he said.
U Mobile said the portable solution also has potential applications in emergency and disaster response.

Its rapid deployment and ability to operate independently of grid power and terrestrial transmission infrastructure could help restore connectivity in areas where existing infrastructure has been disrupted, it said.
27fce163aa956373: SHANGHAI: China's yuan climbed to a three-and-a-half-year high against the dollar on Tuesday after the central bank set a firmer daily fixing for the 10th straight session, the longest streak since late 2023, while investors awaited a meeting between the leaders of the world's two largest economies later this week.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent offered positive comments about the US-China trade relationship ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping's state visit to the US from Sept 23 to 25 at the invitation of President Donald Trump.

While thorny issues like Taiwan may surface, the main focus of their Sept 24 meeting is whether the leaders will signal an extension to a trade truce struck last year that averted a major shock to the global economy.

Senior US and Chinese officials will meet again in about two months in Shenzhen, China, to discuss artificial intelligence dangers and communications protocols in the event of AI safety incidents, Bessent said on Monday.
Prior to the market opening, the People's Bank of China set the midpoint rate at 6.7459 per dollar, its strongest since Feb 3, 2023, but 470 pips weaker than a Reuters' estimate of 6.6989.

The spot yuan is allowed to trade two per cent either side of the fixed midpoint each day. "Ahead of an important Xi-Trump summit, the recent string of stronger fixes could be a show of goodwill and also serves as an anchor for regional currencies in a somewhat volatile environment." Maybank analysts said in a note. "The recent dollar rebound also provides a window for the spot-fix gap to narrow."

In the spot market, the onshore yuan advanced to a high of 6.6936 per dollar at one point, the strongest level since January 2023, before changing hands at 6.6969 as of 0302 GMT. Its offshore counterpart last fetched 6.6965 per dollar.

"The firmer fixing bias is notable given the broader USD/rates backdrop and reinforces the recent shift in fixing guidance towards allowing a somewhat firmer RMB," said Christopher Wong, FX strategist at OCBC Bank.

"This also comes ahead of the Trump-Xi meeting, where we see room for RMB to stay supported into the event." China's yuan has gained about 4.4 per cent against the dollar this year, making it one of Asia's best-performing currencies, supported by resilient exports.
With the yield gap between China and the United States hovering near a record high, some investors expect further yuan appreciation to be more gradual.
"Beyond the meeting, wide US-China yield differentials and soft domestic fundamentals should still limit the pace of RMB appreciation," OCBC's Wong said.

8049b1b049423b92: From Kirstine Vangkilde Berner
The green transition is one of the defining challenges of our time. We know where we need to go. The more difficult question is how we get there, and how we get there fast enough.

Denmark has decades of experience in turning climate ambitions into policies, technologies and business solutions. And we have learnt one thing: governments cannot do it alone. Neither can businesses, researchers or investors. Real progress happens when we bring all players together.

This key question was at the heart of our recent Green Denmark Day in Kuala Lumpur, bringing together around 200 decision-makers, business leaders, experts and investors from Denmark and Malaysia to discuss challenges and possible solutions around green transition, healthy urban living and the future-proofing of food supply.

Across six panel discussions, we explored everything from the energy and water demands of data centres to circular waste systems, healthier cities, preventive healthcare, food security and the potential to turn agricultural side streams into valuable new resources.
These may sound like different conversations. In reality, they are deeply connected.
A growing digital economy creates new demands for energy and water. The way we design cities affects emissions, public health and climate resilience.
Food production depends on water, energy, land and healthy ecosystems. Waste from one industry may become energy, feedstock or raw material for another.
This is why the green transition requires whole-of-society and whole-of-government perspectives. Public-private partnerships are a must.
Collaboration across traditional boundaries has been an important part of Denmark’s own green journey.
Public authorities provide long-term direction and enabling frameworks. Companies develop and deploy solutions. Researchers generate knowledge. Investors help turn ideas into infrastructure.
And there is considerable potential to expand the collaboration on the green transition between Denmark and Malaysia.
Malaysia brings a diversified industrial base, growing digital infrastructure, significant agricultural resources, a dynamic private sector and a strategic position at the heart of Southeast Asia.

Denmark brings experience in renewable energy, energy efficiency, water, sustainable urban development, food, bio-solutions and the circular economy. The potential lies in combining these strengths and creating opportunities for deeper projects, investments and long-term commercial cooperation.

That is precisely why we established the Green Transition Alliance. Alliance brings together the Danish embassy in Malaysia and six Danish companies with capabilities relevant to Malaysia’s green transition: Carlsberg Malaysia, Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners, Novonesis, Novo, Ramboll and Rockwool Malaysia.

Together, the expertise of the companies spans from energy-efficient buildings, industrial decarbonisation, preventive health, bio-solutions, food and agricultural resource efficiency to sustainable cities, infrastructure, renewable energy and investment.

Green Denmark Day opened that ecosystem further by bringing Alliance members together with Malaysian companies, policymakers, researchers, industry associations, investors and other knowledge partners.
The conversations demonstrated why collaboration needs to start with the problem seen from a local context rather than the technology.
Consider data centres. Denmark has successfully captured surplus heat from data centres and used it to heat homes. It is an elegant solution in a cold country.
In tropical Malaysia, there is understandably little demand for district heating. The interesting question is what the Malaysian equivalent might be.

Take waste. Recycling, waste-to-energy, bioenergy and circular design are often presented as competing pathways. But different waste streams require different solutions. The opportunity is to build a system where those solutions complement each other.
Or food. Malaysia is rich in agricultural resources, yet valuable side streams remain underutilised while some inputs are imported.

Fermentation, enzymes and other bio-solutions could create more value from resources already available locally. But technical possibility is not enough. Solutions need consistency, scale and competitive economics.

Healthy cities tell a similar story. Healthcare does not begin at the hospital. It is also shaped by food, buildings, streets, air quality and whether our cities make healthier choices easier for citizens.
No single ministry, company or technology owns these challenges.
Green solutions will scale fastest when sustainability and competitiveness point in the same direction.

Energy efficiency can reduce operating costs. Agricultural side streams can become valuable products. Better-planned cities can become healthier and more attractive places to live and invest. Renewable energy and resilient infrastructure can strengthen energy security.
The green transition should not only be about what we reduce. It should also be about what we create: new industries, capabilities, investments, jobs and partnerships.

Green Denmark Day showed what this can look like. Be honest about what works and what does not. Challenge assumptions. Adapt experience to local realities. Most importantly, leave with a concrete next step.
The Green Transition Alliance is intended to help create more of those next steps.
Because the opportunity before Denmark and Malaysia is not simply to exchange knowledge about the green transition. It is to build it together.
Kirstine Vangkilde Berner is the Danish ambassador to Malaysia.

90c10190f18c0e08: NEW YORK: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in New York on Monday, leading Tehran's diplomatic delegation at the annual gathering of world leaders at the United Nations, the foreign ministry said.
Araghchi is the highest-ranking Iranian official to enter the US since the Middle East war began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February.
Araghchi spoke by phone with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres after his arrival and exchanged views on the agenda of the UN General Assembly, Iranian state television reported.
"Our most important objective is to use a major international platform to defend the legitimacy, rights, and interests of the Iranian people," Araghchi was quoted as telling Iranian journalists.

Earlier, Iranian state media had reported that the Iranian delegation would be led by President Masoud Pezeshkian, and that the US had refused to issue visas to members of his delegation, including his communications team.
However, in a social post on X on Aragchi's arrival in New York, Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei described the minister as "head of a diplomatic delegation" at the General Assembly.
Baqaei said Aragchi "will hold talks and consultations with numerous officials and foreign ministers attending the session."
While the US has authorized an Iranian delegation to travel for the UN gathering, it has, like last year, put restrictions in place.
Iran's delegation will not, for instance, be allowed to purchase luxury goods or other items during their stay in New York City, the State Department said Thursday.
Araghchi left Iran on Sunday evening and had a stopover in Qatar.

Iran says it has conveyed to the US, via Qatar as mediator, conditions for reopening the strategic Strait of Hormuz oil and gas shipping route, which it has effectively choked off since the war began.
The US, in turn, is imposing a counterblockade of Iranian ports.
495b3cdb5cad3673: PETALING JAYA: The investment, trade and industry ministry (Miti) today said it was unaware of the education ministry’s decision to scrap the 30% Bumiputera equity ownership requirement for private education centres.
The education ministry said yesterday that it shelved the controversial prerequisite following discussions with Miti.
However, Miti said matters relating to Bumiputera equity ownership come under the purview of the Economic Planning Unit (EPU), which is under the economy ministry.
"Miti hopes this explanation clarifies the ministry’s role in this matter so that the information conveyed to the public is accurate and clear," it said in a statement.
757f61e9722be843: PETALING JAYA: Pengurus pelaburan kerugian hampir RM1.2 juta selepas individu menyamar sebagai pihak berkuasa mendakwa dirinya terlibat kes pengubahan wang haram dalam kejadian Julai lalu.

Ketua Polis Kelantan Mohd Yusoff Mamat, berkata sindiket penipuan itu dipercayai menggunakan aplikasi penyamaran yang memaparkan nombor telefon, termasuk nombor IPK Kelantan kononnya panggilan itu berasal daripada polis.
Beliau berkata, pihaknya juga sedang menyiasat dengan lebih lanjut susulan mengesan 68 panggilan sehari menggunakan nombor IPK Kelantan.
“Tiada agensi seperti polis atau Bank Negara Malaysia yang menelefon orang awam dan mengarahkan mereka mengeluarkan wang atau membuka akaun baharu.
“Kalau menerima panggilan seperti itu, segera tamatkan panggilan dan hubungi agensi berkaitan melalui saluran rasmi untuk membuat semakan,” katanya menurut Bernama di IPK Kelantan, Kota Bharu.

Mengulas lanjut, Yusoff berkata, mangsa yang juga ibu tunggal berusia 50-an itu mengikut arahan suspek kerana terlalu takut sehingga mengeluarkan wang daripada akaun bank, termasuk simpanan Kumpulan Wang Simpanan Pekerja (KWSP).
Katanya, mangsa juga menggadai dan menjual barang kemas miliknya bernilai hampir RM500,000.
“Wanita itu mengambil masa kira-kira dua bulan untuk membuat laporan polis selepas semua wangnya diserahkan kepada sindiket penipuan berkenaan.
“Dia tahu dirinya tidak terlibat dalam kes pengubahan wang haram tetapi kerana terlalu takut, dia tidak berkongsi perkara itu dengan ahli keluarga atau pihak polis,” katanya.
890a453088e466fb: PETALING JAYA: Timbalan Perdana Menteri, Zahid Hamidi menafikan beliau mendapat perkenan untuk menghadap Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir di Istana Negeri Sembilan di Changkat Persekutuan semalam.
Zahid berkata beliau dan Menteri Besar Negeri Sembilan, Ismail Lasim tidak menerima titah untuk menghadap Tuanku Muhriz dan hanya mengetahui mengenai perkembangan itu menerusi laporan media.
Semalam, Bernama melaporkan beberapa kenderaan, termasuk sebuah yang membawa Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim, tiba di Istana Negeri Sembilan untuk menghadap Tuanku Muhriz.
Pertemuan itu berlaku di tengah-tengah pertikaian mengenai krisis di negeri itu, dengan Bernama melaporkan bahawa Zahid dan Ismail juga dijangka mendapat perkenan menghadap.
"Saya tak ada. Saya dan menteri besar Negeri Sembilan tidak pernah dititah untuk menghadap," kata Zahid hari ini ketika ditanya mengenai pertemuaan itu.
"Kami tahu hanya daripada media saja," katanya kepada pemberita selepas merasmikan Majlis University Research & Innovation Investment Summit 2026.

Zahid juga enggan mengulas lanjut mengenai pertikaian itu, sebaliknya menyerahkan perkara tersebut kepada Ismail. Beliau berkata perkara itu perlu diuruskan dan diselesaikan secara baik di negeri berkenaan.

Katanya, soal interpretasi dalam perundangan dan juga soal kuasa bukan hanya melibatkan taksiran undang-undang, serta menegaskan institusi di Negeri Sembilan perlu dihormati tanpa mengetepikan kedudukan institusi sedia ada.

Perkembangan itu susulan pengumuman Istana Negeri Sembilan bahawa Tuanku Muhriz memutuskan untuk membatalkan pelantikan 10 anggota Majlis Mesyuarat Kerajaan Negeri kerana melanggar sumpah jawatan mereka susulan satu kenyataan bersama yang menyokong penyingkiran baginda sebagai pemerintah negeri.
Mereka mengangkat sumpah dan menandatangani ikrar taat setia pada 7 Ogos lepas.

Bagaimanapun, Ismail semalam mempertikaikan keputusan itu, dengan berkata Perlembagaan Negeri Sembilan tidak membenarkan Yang Dipertuan Besar menamatkan tempoh jawatan seorang anggota exco melainkan atas nasihat atau permintaan menteri besar.
Minggu lalu, exco berkenaan mengeluarkan kenyataan bersama yang didakwa mengesahkan untuk menurunkan Tuanku Muhriz sebagai Yang Dipertuan Besar.
Ismail menyokong kenyataan itu sehari kemudian, walaupun sebelum ini mendakwa bahawa beliau dipaksa menandatangani suatu pengisytiharan untuk menurunkan Tuanku Muhriz.
Dewan Keadilan dan Undang kemudiannya menolak kenyataan exco itu sebagai tidak berperlembagaan dan tidak sah, serta mengesahkan bahawa Tuanku Muhriz kekal sebagai Yang Dipertuan Besar.
c82aaaca7a91b91c: KOTA BHARU, Sept 22 — A company investment manager lost about RM1.2 million after she was duped by a scam syndicate through a phone call in Kota Bharu last July.

Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the woman, a single mother in her 50s, received a call from an individual posing as an authority and claiming that she was involved in a money laundering case.

He said the woman, fearing the consequences, followed the suspect’s instructions, withdrawing money from her bank accounts, including her Employees Provident Fund (EPF) savings, and pawning and selling jewellery worth nearly RM500,000.
“Most concerningly, the woman took about two months before lodging a police report, after all her money had been withdrawn and handed over to the perpetrators.

“She knew that she was not involved in money laundering, but because she was so frightened, she did not tell her family members or the police,” he said in a press conference after the monthly assembly at the Kelantan contingent police headquarters here today.
Mohd Yusoff said the syndicate also used application spoofing technology to make the phone number appear as though the call was from the police, including using the Kelantan IPK’s telephone number.
He said police detected about 68 calls a day using the Kelantan IPK’s number, and the matter was now under investigation.
“Neither the police nor agencies such as Bank Negara Malaysia will call members of the public and instruct them to withdraw money or open a new account.
“If you receive such a call, hang up and contact the relevant agency through its official channels to verify the matter,” he said.
He said police had also sought assistance from Bukit Aman to track down individuals believed to be involved in the scam.
He said the incident began about two months ago before a report was lodged recently and, as of this year, the case was among those involving the largest individual losses recorded in Kelantan.
Meanwhile, Mohd Yusoff said Kelantan police would intensify awareness campaigns through the media to curb commercial crime, which continued to show an increase year-on-year. — Bernama

79dd43474b27cfef: ISTANBUL, Sept 22 — Fifa President Gianni Infantino on Monday sent a letter to Fifa Council members and the presidents of all 211 member associations outlining his openness to dialogue over reform at the world football governing body, Anadolu Ajansi reported, citing The Athletic magazine.

In the letter, seen by The Athletic magazine, Infantino addressed the abandoned Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal and put forward two separate reform plans ahead of the Fifa Council meeting on October 15.

“First, I will ask the Council whether it wishes to commission an independent external review of Fifa’s current governance framework for major strategic initiatives and recommend potential improvements,” Infantino’s letter reads.

“Second, I will propose that the Council establish a direct, structured and time-limited consultation with confederations, Member Associations and relevant stakeholders on how Fifa’s decision-making can be further strengthened.

“The consultation would invite specific proposals on earlier institutional involvement, the respective roles of the President, the Bureau, the Council and the Congress, and practical ways to strengthen transparency, participation and accountability in major strategic initiatives.”
Infantino also stressed that “Fifa’s democratic processes, independence and sporting authority were never for sale.”
“They are not for sale and never will be,” his letter adds.
Regarding the Fifa president’s suggestions for reform, it will be up to the Fifa Council — Fifa’s main decision-making body of 37 members — to decide whether to take the proposals forward.

Infantino has faced growing pressure since launching this summer’s now-abandoned Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal, which involved selling stakes in a company controlling commercial rights to the World Cup and other Fifa competitions to private investors.
The proposal was withdrawn following widespread opposition, but several national associations and continental governing bodies have continued to question Infantino’s leadership. — Bernama-Anadolu
6c5a288cf350cb60: SYDNEY: Australia's corporate watchdog has warned it could take action against "poor practices" by firms in the booming private credit sector, from unrealistic valuations to opaque fees, if standards do not improve.

The sector's rapid growth and complexity have outpaced industry standards, a commissioner of the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) said, saying the recent collapse of property developer Bathla was not surprising.

"The clock is ticking," Commissioner Simone Constant said in a speech in Sydney on Tuesday. "Whether we see broader credit stress or not, certainly the tide is going out on poor private credit practices."
She added, "We're now beyond warnings. The sector should prepare for enforcement action."
The comments come after 18 months of stepped-up scrutiny by ASIC of the industry. The regulator was also surveilling wholesale and retail funds as it pursued enforcement investigations, she added.
"We continue to see issues around valuations, liquidity, governance, conflicts and transparency."
The regulator estimates Australia's private credit sector to be worth about A$200 billion (US$142 billion). It is heavily exposed to real estate lending, making up about 40% to 60% of the market.
Such lending was vulnerable to inflation, cost increases, project delays and unrealistic asset valuations, Constant said.
As a result, fund managers must make difficult decisions when loans deteriorate, she added, rather than "protecting fees or appearance".
Bathla owed A$3 billion to more than 40 lenders when it entered administration, a debt burden administrators said appeared to be a significant contributor to its failure.
"The collapse of Bathla reinforces why strong governance, effective oversight, clear disclosure and accurate valuations are critical," Constant said.
fad6164a709e20ff: NEW YORK: The US on Monday reiterated its commitment to the defense of key Asian allies Japan and South Korea, and the three nations expressed support for Taiwan ahead of a summit this week between US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

Analysts say the US allies are anxious that Trump may offer concessions to Xi including over Taiwan and trade in return for an economic win with Beijing when he hosts Xi at the White House in Washington on Thursday.

Officials say both Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and South Korean President Lee Jae Myung are keen to see the US president during the UN General Assembly in New York, where all three are scheduled to speak on Tuesday.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with his South Korean counterpart Cho Hyun and Japan's Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi in New York on Monday. They issued a joint statement vowing, in apparent reference to China, to stand firm "against economic coercion and non-market policies and practices" and "arbitrary export restrictions that disrupt supply chains."
They also welcomed the launch of a new trilateral consultation mechanism on economic security, part of broader efforts to strengthen supply chains and cooperation on critical technologies.

The statement said the US "reiterated its ironclad commitments to the defense of Japan and the ROK, backed by America’s unmatched military strength, including its nuclear capabilities, and reaffirmed its extended deterrence commitments to Japan and the ROK," using the initials for the Republic of Korea, South Korea's official name.

The statement said the ministers emphasized their commitment to robust security cooperation and the importance of maintaining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait. It also "expressed support for Taiwan's meaningful participation in appropriate international organizations."

In a statement, its foreign ministry said the renewed joint public support for maintaining peace and stability shows that security in the strait has become a "strong consensus of the international community."
Referring to North Korea, the ministers "reaffirmed their resolute commitment to the complete denuclearization of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea" and called on it to resume dialogue.

In addition to concerns about Taiwan, a democratically governed island China claims as its own, analysts said allies will be scrutinizing any trade announcements from the Trump-Xi summit for their impact on competitiveness relative to China. Even a modest reduction in trade barriers for Beijing could erode their positions.

Takaichi angered Beijing last year by saying Tokyo could be drawn into a conflict over Taiwan, and Seoul and Washington have been negotiating details of South Korea's US$350 billion investment package in the US under a trade deal struck by the allies last year.

On Monday, a South Korean opposition lawmaker called for parliamentary scrutiny of the investment package, warning that negotiations over energy projects could leave South Korea carrying disproportionate financial risks.
bc9657a1f7eb7f0c: KUALA LUMPUR: Deputy prime minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has denied being granted an audience at Istana Negeri Sembilan yesterday, saying neither he nor Negeri Sembilan menteri besar Ismail Lasim was summoned to meet Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.

Bernama reported yesterday that several vehicles, including one believed to be carrying Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, arrived at Istana Negeri Sembilan in Changkat Persekutuan for an audience with Tuanku Muhriz.
The reported meeting came amid a dispute over Tuanku Muhriz’s position as the state ruler, with Bernama reporting that Zahid and Ismail were also expected to be granted an audience.
"I wasn't there," Zahid said today when asked to comment on the meeting.

"The menteri besar and I were not summoned for an audience, and we only found out about it through reports in the media," he said when met by reporters after officiating the University Research and Innovation Investment Summit 2026 here.
Zahid declined to comment further on the political dispute, deferring to Ismail. He said the matter should be managed and resolved amicably within the state.

He also said the dispute involved complex legal interpretations concerning powers and constitutional jurisdiction, and stressed that state institutions and the royal framework in Negeri Sembilan must be respected.

This follows the Negeri Sembilan palace’s announcement that Tuanku Muhriz had decided to revoke the appointments of 10 state executive councillors for violating their oath of office following a joint statement that endorsed his removal as the state ruler.
The palace said the exco members were also found to have breached their pledge of allegiance to the Yang Dipertuan Besar, which they took on Aug 7.
It said that under the state’s constitution, exco members other than the menteri besar hold office at the ruler's pleasure.

Ismail yesterday disputed Tuanku Muhriz’s decision to revoke the appointments, saying Negeri Sembilan’s constitution does not allow the state ruler to terminate the tenure of an exco member unless advised or requested by the menteri besar.
Last week, the exco released a joint statement purportedly affirming Tuanku Muhriz’s removal as Yang Dipertuan Besar.
Ismail endorsed the statement a day later, despite previously claiming that he was coerced into signing a proclamation on Tuanku Muhriz’s alleged removal.
The Negeri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang dismissed the exco’s statement as unconstitutional and invalid, affirming that Tuanku Muhriz remained the state’s ruler.
The Attorney-General’s Chambers also said the statement had no legal effect as the menteri besar and his exco do not have the power to unilaterally vacate the state ruler’s position.
bf966d7e0d3d34c7: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 22 — Penang is seeking the federal government’s support through Budget 2027 to strengthen its tourism agenda, including improving air connectivity, attracting more international events and preserving George Town’s heritage.

State Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said the priorities were aimed at increasing the value of the tourism sector while ensuring its growth continued to benefit the local economy and community.

He said one of the main priorities was an international air connectivity fund, including matching grants, to attract more direct flights to Penang from strategic markets such as Japan, South Korea, Australia and the Middle East.

“With the Penang International Airport (LTAPP) upgrading project set to double its capacity to 12 million passengers a year, the priority now is to ensure that the capacity can be fully utilised through new routes and increased flight frequencies,” he told Bernama.
The LTAPP expansion and upgrading project is expected to be completed in June 2028, according to reports.

Wong said Penang was also seeking a larger federal matching fund to bid for and attract international conferences, exhibitions, sporting events, festivals, concerts, as well as large-scale arts and cultural events.

He said business events generated an economic impact of about RM1.91 billion last year, demonstrating Penang’s potential to become a major regional hub for business and major events with its new facilities and increased capacity.
The fund could also be used to develop creative content, productions, local festivals and intellectual property that could be brought to the international stage, he said.
Wong also proposed that the government establish a Unesco George Town Conservation and Regeneration Fund to ensure the heritage city continues to thrive as a living heritage city.

He said dedicated allocations were needed for the conservation of heritage buildings, enhancement of public spaces, safety and accessibility, as well as the preservation of traditional businesses, artisans and communities that make George Town a living heritage city.

“We do not want to merely preserve buildings. We need to ensure that the heritage, culture and local communities continue to thrive while being able to generate new economic activities through tourism and the creative economy,” he said.
Wong said Penang’s focus after Visit Malaysia 2026 should shift from pursuing tourist numbers to high-value tourism.
Meanwhile, he called for the formula of channelling 100 per cent of tourism tax to the states in 2026 to be continued next year.
“As Visit Malaysia has been extended to 2027, it is hoped that the 100 per cent allocation of tourism tax can also be continued next year,” he said.
Budget 2027 is expected to be tabled by Prime Minister, who is also Finance Minister, Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, on Oct 9. — Bernama
edc82f0e18d29517: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 22 — A 37-year-old man who allegedly threw his five-year-old niece into a river in Kampung Padang, Tanjung Sedili here, causing her death yesterday, has been remanded for seven days to assist in the investigation.
Sessions Court Judge Hafizah Abdul Rajak granted the police’s remand application until September 28 to facilitate investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
The suspect, who had been receiving treatment at Kota Tinggi Hospital, arrived at the court complex at 9am today, escorted by policemen.
It was reported yesterday that police arrested a local man for allegedly throwing his niece into a river, resulting in her death.
Kota Tinggi police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said police received a report at about 9.30am before arresting the suspect.
The suspect, who was also the deceased girl’s uncle, allegedly threw the victim into the river before going on a rampage while armed with a machete and chasing the victim’s 40-year-old father.
A police officer was also injured during a struggle while attempting to apprehend the suspect.
Police are still investigating the motive behind the incident, while the suspect is believed to have mental health issues.
The victim’s body was sent to Pasir Gudang Hospital and is expected to be buried in Kampung Sayang here after the post-mortem examination is completed.
