2af0d7f1d6ac4172: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — After more than 15 years of making films independently in Malaysia, brothers Iskander Azizuddin and Feisal Azizuddin are taking Feisk Productions to the next stage after being selected for an international film residency in Los Angeles.

The co-founders of the Malaysian production company are among nine Malaysians selected for the 2026 Global Media Makers (GMM) LA Residency, which brings together film and television professionals from across Asia and connects them with the US industry.

Implemented by Film Independent in partnership with the US Department of State’s Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs, GMM offers mentorship, masterclasses and project development sessions covering areas such as financing, distribution and the business of film and television.
The programme, running from September 12 to October 3, also includes participants from Indonesia, Japan, South Korea and Thailand.
For Feisk, the timing comes as the company begins to see more of its work move beyond Malaysia.

Its upcoming feature Curi Makan, internationally titled Ali & Ben’s Spicy Meats, was recently picked up by Kuala Lumpur-based Abnormal Studios for worldwide sales, allowing the cannibal black comedy-horror to reach international buyers.
The deal follows the company’s earlier experience taking Angkat overseas.
The family conflict drama had its world premiere at the Blue Chair Film Festival in Luang Prabang, Laos, in 2024, after going through development on regional platforms.

These projects form part of a wider body of work built by Feisk since it was founded in 2010, with the company producing feature films, television, documentaries and short films across a range of genres.
The GMM residency now allows Iskander and Feisal to look beyond the production side of filmmaking and better understand how projects can be financed, developed and distributed internationally.
It also places them alongside filmmakers from the region with experience in some of the world’s major film festivals.

Among the international participants are Thai producer Kissada Kamyoung, whose work includes 9 Temples to Heaven, and Indonesian filmmaker Khozy Rizal, whose films, including Little Rebels Cinema Club, have screened at international film festivals.
The other members of the Malaysian delegation reflect the range of the country’s screen industry.
They include Fareeq Alias, a creative director and filmmaker whose documentary Pekik won Best Documentary at the 33rd Festival Filem Malaysia.
Zan Azlee, a journalist, documentary filmmaker and Berlinale Talents alumnus, has produced non-fiction work in conflict zones and politically complex environments across Asia and the Middle East.

Benjamin Sevang has built a career in television production with major broadcasters including TV3 and Astro, while Lemuel Ong is a writer, producer and senior production executive at Astro with experience in content development and production.
Perassath Servai is a filmmaker and multidisciplinary artist whose work explores Malaysian Indian identity, gender and social stereotypes.
The delegation also includes filmmakers Iris Chia and Nora Nabila.
d77ebca1ed8d5301: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 22 — Wage compression is hindering working Malaysians from receiving proper compensation despite the narrowing wage gap between low- and semi-skilled workers in Malaysia, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said today.
Citing a recent Bank Negara report, Akmal Nasrullah said the wage difference between low- and semi-skilled workers had narrowed from RM550 in 2016 to RM396 in 2024.

“This means the wage is moving (upwards) at the minimum wage level but comparatively, it is not progressing as well in the successive levels,” he said during the ministry’s monthly assembly at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) today.
As such, he said raising the floor wage was only a starting point and the ministry must develop clearer wage ladders that keep pace with productivity.
Akmal Nasrullah also pointed out that only four states and federal territories had surpassed the national median monthly wage of RM2,940, namely Penang, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya.

The ministry, he said, had decided to allocate higher development allocations to six states and territories — Kedah, Perlis, Kelantan, Terengganu, Sabah and Sarawak — to support them in also crossing the RM2,940 mark.

While noting that Malaysia’s inflation remained moderate at 1.9 per cent, Akmal Nasrullah said managing cost-of-living pressures was essential for working Malaysians to benefit from salary progressions.
Malaysia last raised the minimum wage from RM1,500 to RM1,700 per month in August 2025 and seeks to scale it up to RM3,000 per month by 2030 under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP).
6b169305676d988b: SEPTEMBER 22 — A few days ago, while I was settling into my office at UM Press, my secretary sent me a WhatsApp message.
“Prof, gentle reminder. Meeting with the Faculty of Law management at 2.30 pm today to discuss the faculty’s book publishing strategy.”
I replied with a simple, “Noted. Thanks.”
The rest of the day unfolded very much as expected. There were emails waiting to be answered, manuscripts to review, a couple of phone calls in between, and, of course, the meeting itself.

We discussed publishing plans, possible book titles and series (and a co-publication opportunity with an international publisher), timelines and the kinds of manuscripts that might interest a wider (non-law) audience.
Tea and sandwiches were served. I cracked a joke that made everyone laugh. Before long, the meeting ended and everyone hurried off to the next appointment waiting in their calendars.
If you had walked into the room that afternoon, you probably would not have noticed anything unusual about me. I doubt anyone else in the room did either.
It had only been nineteen days since Mak passed away.

Even writing that sentence now feels strangely unreal. Nineteen days is hardly enough time for life to make sense again, yet it is apparently long enough for meetings to resume, emails to keep arriving, and WhatsApp reminders to continue appearing on the screen as though nothing has changed.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
For the writer, ordinary routines continued even as he was grieving the loss of his mother. — Pexels pic

Students still submitting their appeals for next semester’s accommodation, even if the deadline has long gone. Television producers and newspaper editors still call. Authors still ask when their books will be ready. The supermarket still runs out of the brand of Greek yoghurt we normally buy.
Life, it seems, is remarkably consistent in continuing with its ordinary routines.
I have come to realise that this is not life being insensitive. It is simply life doing what it has always done.
The calendar does not know that we are grieving. The clock does not pause because someone we love is no longer here.

Every new day quietly arrives, asking only for the next small thing. Another meeting appears on the calendar, another email lands in the inbox, another manuscript needs editing, and another drive to work begins.
Somewhere along the way, without ever making a conscious decision, we begin answering those requests one by one.
That afternoon, I genuinely enjoyed the discussion with our colleagues from the Faculty of Law. We exchanged ideas, debated publishing strategies and laughed together more than once.
None of it felt forced, and none of it felt like I was pretending to be someone I was not.

It has taken me a little while to understand that it is entirely possible to miss someone deeply and still find something genuinely funny. It is possible to carry grief into a meeting without making the meeting about grief.
Those experiences do not cancel each other out. They simply learn to exist within the same ordinary day.
The experience also made me wonder how often we misread the people around us.

We see someone smiling and assume life must be treating them kindly. We hear a cheerful voice on the telephone and imagine everything is going well. We watch a colleague confidently chair a meeting and conclude that they have everything under control.
Yet we rarely know what someone carried into the room before greeting us.

The young colleague having teh ais across the table may still be learning how to leave a toxic relationship behind. The receptionist who cheerfully says good morning may be worrying about an elderly parent. The Grab driver asking about your day may have a child sitting for examinations.
Or perhaps the person discussing book publishing strategies with you buried the only mother he will ever have just nineteen days earlier.
The older I become, the less convinced I am that strength is something we can recognise from the outside.

Many of the strongest people I know never speak about what they are carrying. They continue showing up because other people are depending on them, because responsibilities still need to be fulfilled, or simply because they understand that everyone else is carrying something unseen as well.
What looks like composure is often nothing more than quiet perseverance, repeated one ordinary day after another.

Tomorrow morning another WhatsApp reminder will almost certainly appear before I have finished my first cup of coffee. I will probably reply, “Noted. Thanks,” just as I always do, before getting on with another ordinary day.
The work will continue, the meetings will continue, and so, I suspect, will life itself.
Mak has already left me with many gifts over the years, but perhaps this is one more that I never expected.
Some of the heaviest things people carry are also the things we cannot see.

514490626461bf2b: BEIJING: Alibaba Group Holding is rolling out what it calls China’s most powerful AI chip, an accelerator to compete with Nvidia and underpin a massive expansion of data centre capacity in coming years.

The ecommerce company turned AI-aspirant on Tuesday outlined a new Zhenwu V900 accelerator that it says triples the performance of its predecessor. From Alibaba’s T-Head chip division, it can be combined in clusters of up to 500,000 units to power frontier-model training, CEO Eddie Wu said.

Alibaba is among the biggest spenders on AI among leading Chinese players. It’s committed to spending more than US$53 billion over a three-year period to expand its AI capabilities, and raised about US$10.2 billion from a follow-on share offering in Hong Kong in August.
On Tuesday, Wu set a target of 20 gigawatts of data centre capacity for its Alibaba Cloud service by 2032, on the expectation of “exponentially rising demand for AI.”
Wu spoke as global AI stocks rallied on early signs of success for Meta Platforms Inc.’s new personal agent, reviving investor optimism after recent market uncertainty.
Alibaba has pledged to intensify its expenditure on AI hardware and infrastructure as Wu’s leadership team makes the pursuit of artificial general intelligence the company’s lodestar.
It also plans to list the T-Head chip design unit to tap interest in the white-hot AI accelerator market, Bloomberg News has reported.
The company now plans to develop a model with between 5 and 10 trillion parameters, far larger than what’s common today, which would be designed to handle longer and more complex tasks.
The CEO’s plans contrast with recent warnings from top AI labs in the US, after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei urged a slower pace of development to better handle AI risks.
Alibaba’s event comes on the eve of a summit between US president Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping this week, when the leaders will discuss a swathe of issues.
AI matters are set to figure prominently, as top-level US executives like Nvidia boss Jensen Huang and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella will attend a White House state dinner with the national leaders.

2fb14404631f0865: HONG KONG: Bitcoin retreated from an eight-month high Tuesday in Asia after a dizzying rally that saw it surge more than 13% in four days.

The original cryptocurrency eased to around US$85,500 in early Singapore trading from as high as $87,381 in the US session, still up around US$10,000 from last week’s lows after crypto joined a broad rebound in risk assets including stocks. Bitcoin is back at late-January levels but remains well below its record of US$126,000 set in October.

“The rapid move back through US$80,000 has traders believing the bear phase is over; momentum is bringing sidelined capital back in, so the path of least resistance is higher,” said Rich Rosenblum, co-founder of crypto market maker GSR. “The risk is that this is a macro liquidity trade wearing a crypto costume. If so, a risk-assets wobble would put Bitcoin under significant pressure.”

Digital assets have brushed off last week’s failure of landmark US legislation that would have established clearer industry regulation and the Federal Reserve’s first interest-rate increase in more than three years. A green light on Thursday from the Securities and Exchange Commission for blockchain-based versions of securities to start trading in the US brightened the mood, sending related tokens soaring.
Falling oil prices and optimism ahead of a summit between US president Donald Trump and China’s Xi Jinping have buoyed markets more broadly.

Liquidations of long and short positions across digital assets have climbed to more than US$1 billion over the last 24 hours, with short bets accounting for about US$840 million of that, according to data compiled by Coinglass.

“It looks like mechanics before conviction. Bitcoin cleared the top of its September range into a dense band of short liquidation levels, and forced buying did the rest,” said Rachael Lucas, an analyst at BTC Markets. “US$84,000 is the level that matters. It was the breakout, and it should now hold as the floor if this is a regime change rather than a short squeeze.”

Bitcoin open interest on the options trading platform Deribit was heavily dominated by calls, signalling bullish sentiment. The platform showed nearly 320,000 contracts for the right to buy the token compared with over 169,000 for puts, or the right to sell.

Other positives lifting sentiment around Bitcoin are big inflows into spot US exchange-traded funds at the end of last week and Michael Saylor’s Strategy - the largest corporate holder of Bitcoin - purchasing the token for the first time in three weeks.
Still, headwinds remain, with crude oil at around US$100 a barrel and US Treasury yields elevated, though falling.

Bitcoin is still off its 2026 high of over US$97,000 in mid-January, and retail enthusiasm has proven hard to rekindle as artificial intelligence stocks and other AI-linked trades compete for the same pool of speculative capital.

“For most of this year crypto was the forgotten macro trade, it lagged equities and gold while capital and attention moved to AI,” said Rosenblum. “What’s changed is positioning, not fundamentals: Bitcoin was under-owned and leaning short.”
7701e3c6a753cdee: SEOUL: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung has urged the United States to ease sanctions on North Korea in exchange for an agreement under which Pyongyang would freeze its nuclear weapons programmes, the New York Times reported.

"I believe there is significant value in a trade-off between sanctions – which are not particularly effective anyway – and a stop to the development of additional nuclear weapons and intercontinental ballistic missile technology," the newspaper quoted Lee as saying in an interview.

"Once it believes it has accumulated enough nuclear weapons and missiles to guarantee its survival, it will be tempted to export them to make money," he said. "That will be a truly dangerous moment."

South Korean officials have said that they are moving away from a "denuclearisation first" policy in favour ‌of a "peace first" approach towards North Korea, with Lee pledging ‌last ⁠year to respect North Korea's system and seek peaceful coexistence with Pyongyang.

Relations between the Koreas remain frozen, however. North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has abandoned Pyongyang's reunification ​policy, describing ​the South ⁠as its most hostile state and ordering stronger frontline defences.
US President Donald Trump is seeking to hold a new meeting with Kim, and the South Korean president has said that he is keen to see the talks happen.
Lee intends to present his vision for peace and coexistence on the Korean Peninsula to the UN this week during the UN General Assembly.

d378e0fdbaab3978: PUTRAJAYA: Mahkamah Rayuan akan memutuskan pada 7 Jan depan berkait cabaran Badan Peguam terhadap keputusan Lembaga Pengampunan Wilayah Persekutuan (LPWP) pada 2024 yang memotong hukuman penjara bekas perdana menteri, Najib Razak dan pengurangan denda kes SRC International.

Keputusan itu dibuat selepas LPWP memberikan pengampunan bersyarat kepada Najib minggu lalu, yang membenarkannya menjalani baki hukuman di bawah tahanan rumah sehingga 23 Ogos 2028, tertakluk kepada pembayaran denda RM50 juta.

Peguam Badan Peguam Rajpal Singh Ghai, berkata pendaftar Mahkamah Rayuan memaklumkan kepada pihak terlibat mengenai tarikh keputusan 7 Jan itu kira-kira dua minggu lalu, sebelum LPWP memberikan pengampunan bersyarat terbaru kepada Najib.

Panel tiga hakim terdiri Hakim Lim Chong Fong, Azhahari Kamal Ramli, dan Leonard David Shim mendengar rayuan Badan Peguam pada 31 Julai , berhubung keengganan Mahkamah Tinggi memberikan kebenaran untuk semakan kehakiman.
Badan Peguam berhasrat membatalkan keputusan dibuat 2024 itu, selain mendapatkan pengisytiharan bahawa ia tidak sah, tidak mengikut Perlembagaan, dan terbatal.
Ketika pendengaran tersebut, peguam Yeo Yang Poh berhujah kebertanggungjawaban merupakan tonggak utama sistem keadilan, dan keputusan LPWP sepatutnya tertakluk penelitian kehakiman.
"LPWP mesti bertanggungjawab kepada rakyat. Jadi, keputusannya mesti tertakluk kepada semakan kehakiman dan pintu mahkamah tidak sepatutnya ditutup," katanya.
Yeo berkata, ambang untuk mendapatkan kebenaran adalah rendah dengan Badan Peguam telah mengemukakan kes yang mempunyai asas hujah serta bukannya remeh atau menyusahkan.
Bekas presiden Badan Peguam, Zainur Zakaria, berhujah pindaan Perlembagaan pada 1994 telah menghapuskan kuasa budi bicara mutlak Yang di-Pertuan Agong dalam menjalankan fungsi Perlembagaannya.
Beliau merujuk Perkara 40(1A) menghendaki baginda bertindak mengikut nasihat apabila menjalankan fungsi tersebut.
Membantah rayuan berkenaan, Peguam Kanan Persekutuan Ahmad Hanir Hambaly, berkata Mahkamah Tinggi wajar menolak kebenaran kerana perkara itu tidak boleh diadili di mahkamah.
Beliau berkata, cabaran itu menyentuh hak prerogatif Yang di-Pertuan Agong mengikut Perkara 42 Perlembagaan Persekutuan, yang tidak tertakluk kepada semakan kehakiman.

Peguam Najib, Shafee Abdullah, menyokong hujah kerajaan sambil menegaskan keputusan akhir mengenai pengampunan terletak pada Yang di-Pertuan Agong, manakala ahli lembaga hanya mengemukakan pandangan mereka.
LPWP mengurangkan hukuman asal penjara 12 tahun Najib kepada enam tahun dan denda daripada RM210 juta kepada RM50 juta, pada Januari 2024.
Di bawah pengampunan bersyarat minggu lalu, Najib mesti mematuhi syarat dikenakan atau berdepan risiko pengampunan itu dibatalkan dan beliau dihantar semula ke penjara.
Keputusan Mahkamah Rayuan itu akan menentukan sama ada Badan Peguam boleh meneruskan cabaran substantifnya terhadap keputusan pada 2024 berkenaan.
0fcafdab63cca01e: IPOH: An Orang Asli man was killed in what was believed to be a tiger attack while searching for rattan with a friend in the Korbu forest reserve near Kampung Takung, Pos Perwor, Sungai Siput, yesterday.

c1295ce3f8097f00: SINGAPORE: Technology stocks powered Asian markets higher on Tuesday as lower oil prices lifted sentiment and investors pinned their hopes on US-Iran talks, while the dollar stood tall on bets that more hikes are needed to rein in inflation.

Attention is also turning to a high-stakes meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping later this week, with investors watching for signs the leaders of the world's two largest economies can prevent a further deterioration in relations.

Xi arrives in Washington on Wednesday for the first time in more than a decade amid growing optimism that a trade truce deal between the two nations will be extended and potential cooperation over artificial intelligence.
Brent crude futures steadied at US$100.22 per barrel after dropping over 3% in the previous session, moving below the key US$100 level briefly.

President Trump said he would be open to meeting Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian, who is expected to be in New York this week for the UN General Assembly, helping lift sentiment and pushing bond yields lower.
"The drop in oil is a big factor," said Nick Twidale, chief market strategist at ATFX Global. "Oil is the main driver and investors are jumping back into AI as has been the pattern this year."

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rose over 1% in early trading. Tech-heavy South Korean stocks jumped nearly 2% while Taiwan shares were 1.3% higher. Japan markets are closed for a holiday.
Nasdaq futures rose 0.37% while European futures were 0.3% higher. Much of the AI enthusiasm has been centred on the strong reception to the launch of Meta's Muse AI assistant.
China's blue-chip stock index rose 0.75%, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng index gained 0.4%. AI stocks in China and Hong Kong also surged.
"The excitement around Meta Muse is adding weight to the idea that millions of people could eventually use persistent AI agents," said Chris Weston, head of research at Pepperstone.

"The combination of Meta Muse injecting a new shot of confidence in the CPU demand profile, lower crude prices, falling Treasury yields and optimism towards the US-China summit have supported the move."

Investors are also contending with a fresh wave of rate hikes and hawkish signals from major central banks, reinforcing expectations of further tightening later this year. The shift has underpinned the dollar and piled pressure on the yen.
The yen was at 157.39 per US dollar, hovering near a three-week low after surrendering early-month gains driven by bets on a faster pace of Bank of Japan rate hikes.
The BOJ raised rates last week to a 31-year high but two dissenting votes and lack of explicit hawkish guidance disappointed investors, leaving the yen vulnerable and stoking intervention jitters.

"FX intervention remains a blunt tool to prop up currencies, and without a forceful monetary policy response it will be difficult for Japanese authorities to rein in the selloff in the yen," said Matthew Ryan, head of market strategy at Ebury.
The Federal Reserve, by contrast, raised rates last week and warned its fight against inflation was not over, keeping the door open to further tightening.

The dollar index, which measures the US currency against six other units, was at 100.4, just shy of a seven-week high. Traders are pricing in a 56% chance of a hike in October, compared with 43.5% a week earlier, CME FedWatch tool showed.

6b2b12cac149952d: PARIS: The 2026/27 Nations League kicks off on Thursday, but all eyes will be on the touchlines as a starry cast of new coaches, including Zinedine Zidane and Jurgen Klopp, prepare to make their debuts in international football.

The end of World Cup cycles usually herald in a host of new faces, however, the 2026 vintage is particularly bountiful, with no fewer than 10 European nations having appointed a new coach since this summer's tournament in North America.
Most notable are 1998 World Cup winner and France legend Zidane, who succeeds Didier Deschamps as Les Bleus boss, and former Liverpool manager Klopp, who takes over his native Germany.
When Deschamps announced the 2026 World Cup would signal the end of his 14-year reign as France boss, only one name was on the lips of football fans in the country: 'Zizou'.
They got their wish when it was announced in July that the three-time Champions League-winning coach was replacing his old team-mate and captain at the helm of Les Bleus.
"It's like a film, but it's amazing. It's real," current France skipper Kylian Mbappe told Spanish daily AS on Monday.

Finally, the 54-year-old will oversee his first matches as coach away to Turkey on Friday and in Belgium three days later, before making his touchline bow at the Stade de France on Oct 2 against Italy.
A second meeting against the Belgians in Paris the following Monday will bring the curtain down on Zidane's opening salvo in international management.
"The France job was the only one I wanted," former Real Madrid coach Zidane said in July.
"I've had offers over these four or five years to take charge of a club, and I turned them all down for the French national team.
"I'm ready for the challenge, that's what drives me."
'The high point'

If Zidane's appointment marks the long-awaited return of an iconic figure to the national team in France, Klopp's has been greeted with no less excitement in Germany, even if it is the former Mainz defender's first taste of the Nationalmannschaft.

Uncapped as a player, Klopp made his name in football as a coach. After legendary spells at Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool, and a period away from the touchline as Red Bull's global sports director, Klopp will begin an adventure many in Germany thought would never happen.

"This is ideally the high point of my career, of my life, my professional life. I will give it everything I have," Klopp said at his unveiling after Julian Nagelsmann departed following Germany's disastrous World Cup.
The charismatic 59-year-old Klopp has already shown he will do things his way by calling up 44 players, divided into two squads, for his first matches in charge.
Those games will be against the Netherlands in Amsterdam on Thursday and at home to Greece three days later, before a meeting with Serbia in Munich on October 1 and a trip to Greece on Oct 4.
Other arrivals for this opening round of Nations League matches include Jorge Jesus, who will make his Portugal debut when the competition's reigning champions welcome Wales on Thursday.
Ex-Barcelona metronome and 2010 World Cup winner Xavi Hernandez replaces Ronald Koeman as Netherlands coach.
Roberto Mancini, who masterminded Italy's Euro 2020 victory, returns to try and right the course of the floundering Azzurri.

Former Bayern Munich and Netherlands midfielder Mark van Bommel will oversee his first Belgium match against Italy, and Slaven Bilic takes over the Croatia reins for a second time, following a successful six-year spell in charge of the Vatreni between 2006 and 2012.
Spain's World Cup and European Championship-winning coach Luis de la Fuente is staying put. He was on Monday rewarded with a contract extension until 2032.
His world champions will begin their tilt at a second Nations League title with an eye-catching clash against Thomas Tuchel's England at Wembley on Saturday.
93f40c4cc998d24f: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal will rule on Jan 7 on the Malaysian Bar’s challenge to the Federal Territories Pardons Board’s (FTPB) 2024 decision to halve former prime minister Najib Razak’s jail term and reduce his fine in the SRC International case.

The decision comes after the FTPB granted Najib a conditional pardon last week, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to the payment of a RM50 million fine.
Bar counsel Rajpal Singh Ghai said the Court of Appeal registry informed the parties of the Jan 7 decision date about two weeks ago, before the FTPB granted Najib the latest conditional pardon.

A three-member bench comprising Justices Lim Chong Fong, Azhahari Kamal Ramli and Leonard David Shim heard the Bar’s appeal on July 31 against the High Court’s refusal to grant leave for judicial review.
The Bar is seeking to quash the 2024 decision and obtain a declaration that it was unlawful, unconstitutional and void.
During the hearing, lawyer Yeo Yang Poh argued that accountability was a fundamental pillar of the justice system, and that the FTPB’s decision should be subject to judicial scrutiny.
"The FTPB must be held accountable to the people. As such, its decisions must be susceptible to judicial review, and the doors of the court must not be shut," he said.
Yeo said the threshold for leave was low and that the Bar had raised an arguable case that was neither frivolous nor vexatious.
Former Bar president Zainur Zakaria argued that a 1994 constitutional amendment had removed the Yang di-Pertuan Agong’s absolute discretion in exercising his constitutional functions.
He relied on Article 40(1A), which requires the king to act in accordance with advice when exercising such functions.
Opposing the appeal, senior federal counsel Ahmad Hanir Hambaly said the High Court was right to refuse leave as the matter was non-justiciable.
He said the challenge concerned the Yang di-Pertuan Agong’s prerogative under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution, which was not amenable to judicial review.

Najib’s lawyer, Shafee Abdullah, adopted the government’s submissions, arguing that the final decision on a pardon rests with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, while members of the board merely offer their views.
The FTPB reduced Najib’s original 12-year sentence to six years and his RM210 million fine to RM50 million in January 2024.
Under last week’s conditional pardon, Najib must comply with the conditions imposed or risk having the pardon revoked and being returned to prison.
The Court of Appeal’s ruling will determine whether the Bar can proceed with its substantive challenge to the 2024 decision.
be8a807faa377f99: KUALA LUMPUR: The Indian high commission in Kuala Lumpur has warned Indian nationals against using Malaysia’s 30-day visa-free facility to seek employment.

It said using the facility to seek employment would be a clear violation of immigration rules.
"There is a noticeable increase in Indian nationals arriving in Malaysia using the 30-day visa-free facility to seek employment.
"The high commission of India in Kuala Lumpur alerts Indian nationals travelling to Malaysia on tourist visas against taking up employment.
"Many Indian nationals are misled by unscrupulous agents with false job promises, leading to overstays, illegal status, exploitation, detention and legal action," it said.
The high commission also reiterated that Indian nationals should not travel to Malaysia for employment without a valid work permit or visa with reference.

It said genuine tourists must carry valid and verifiable documentation such as confirmed return tickets, hotel bookings, online submissions of the Malaysia digital arrival card three days before the arrival date, and passports with a minimum six-month validity to avoid immigration-related issues on arrival in Malaysia.

b4066872d40aeb76: Australians can’t afford to be complacent – Pauline Hanson also thinks it’s OK to shut out reporters she doesn’t like No politician loves journalists. 50573288f8ccffde: Bolehkah Menteri Besar Negeri Sembilan Ismail Lasim dilihat telah mengambil langkah direct confrontation terhadap rajanya yakni Yang Dipertuan Besar?
Jika boleh, maknanya krisis Negeri Sembilan yang sudah berlarutan menuju tahap lebih serius, lebih rumit, lebih parah. Mungkin sudah pun begitu keadaannya.
Tetapi adakah Ismail memang telah ambil langkah 'pertentangan terbuka' terhadap Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir in the first place? It certainly looks so.

Imbau apa yang berlaku sehari dua ini. Pada Ahad 20 Sept lalu kenyataan dikeluarkan Pengelola Bijaya Diraja Istana Negeri Sembilan Azizi Mohamad Ali memaklumkan Yang Dipertuan Besar membatalkan pelantikan Ahli-ahli Majlis Mesyuarat Kerajaan Negeri (exco) berkuat kuasa serta-merta.
Pada Isnin 21 Sept, menteri besar pula keluarkan kenyataan memberitahu "semua exco kerajaan Negeri Sembilan sedia ada adalah sah dan akan menjalankan tugas masing-masing seperti biasa".
Kenyataan menteri besar sekali gus menolak apa yang telah dilaksanakan oleh Yang Dipertuan Besar. Bak kata tajuk laporan Malaysiakini "N Sembilan MB rejects Tuanku Muhriz's firing of excos".

Menurut Pengelola Bijaya Diraja Istana, keputusan Yang Dipertuan Besar dibuat setelah mendapati semua 10 exco terbabit memungkir sumpah jawatan. Umum tahu mereka mengangkat sumpah dan menandatangani ikrar taat setia pada 7 Ogos lalu sebelum dilantik sebagai exco. Namun umum juga tahu pada 15 Sept mereka membuat keputusan kolektif bahawa proklamasi penurunan takhta Tuanku Muhriz sebagai Yang Dipertuan Besar adalah sah.

Ahli exco juga mengiktiraf Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Jaafar sebagai Yang Dipertuan Besar yang baharu berkuat kuasa serta-merta. Dengan berbuat demikian pihak istana melihat mereka memungkiri sumpah setia.

Menteri besar menyifatkan tindakan melucutkan jawatan barisan exco 'tidak berperlembagaan'. Pihak istana pula menyatakan tindakan berlandaskan Undang-undang Tubuh Kerajaan Negeri Sembilan yang ada memperuntukkan seseorang ahli MMKN memegang jawatan selagi diperkenan Yang Dipertuan Besar.

Apa pun, jujur saya katakan apabila Tuanku Muhriz membatalkan pelantikan barisan exco negeri, anggapan saya ialah Yang Dipertuan Besar akhirnya telah stamped his foot setelah sekian lama berdiam diri. Menerusi tindakan itu, Yang Dipertuan Besar memberitahu semua pihak yang mengganggu-gugat pemerintahan dan memaksanya turun takhta bahawa enough is enough.
Dengan itu, pada hemat saya (sebenarnya harapan saya) krisis Negeri Sembilan akan ditamatkan.

Perlu dinyatakan juga kebelakangan ini pendirian menteri besar yang berubah-ubah tidak membantu menyelesaikan masalah, malah merumitkan. Tidak perlulah saya huraikan flip-flop yang dilakukan atas dua sebab. Satu, ramai sudah tahu. Dua, ceritanya panjang dan akan buat artikel berjela-jela.
Bagaimanapun, perlu dinyatakan selain institusi adat, Umno yakni parti menteri besar juga pemain utama krisis ini.

Ingat 27 April lalu? Hari itu Umno Negeri Sembilan menarik balik sokongan terhadap Aminuddin Harun sebagai menteri besar sambil mendakwa tidak puas hati terhadap cara beliau mengendalikan pertikaian para undang dan pemerintah. Kemelut undang tercetus tahun sebelumnya.
Adun Umno merancang bentuk kerajaan negeri yang baharu dengan sokongan PAS-Perikatan Nasional ala tebuk atap. Namun Tuanku Muhriz dilapor enggan menerima menghadap Umno.

Sebaliknya, Aminuddin ditugaskan oleh pemerintah untuk mengetuai kerajaan minoriti. Memendekkan cerita yang panjang beliau terpaksa juga bubar DUN dengan perkenan Tuanku Muhriz untuk memberi laluan pilihan raya negeri diadakan.

Umno bekerjasama dengan PAS. Naratif mereka: kerajaan pimpinan Aminuddin gagal menangani krisis istana dan tidak boleh diharapkan untuk mempertahan institusi raja. Juga dimainkan ialah politik identiti. Umno menang pilihan raya yang diadakan 1 Ogos lalu lantas bentuk kerajaan.

Pada 17 Sept lalu bekas ahli Majlis Kerja Tertinggi Umno Puad Zarkashi dipetik portal The Vibes mengutarakan pertanyaan sama ada Umno Negeri Sembilan sedang dilanda internal split berikutan kontroversi berhubung proklamasi berkaitan kedudukan Yang Dipertuan Besar.

"Adakah benar wujud dua puak dalam Umno Negeri Sembilan?" tanya Puad. Beliau tidak menyebut nama sesiapa. Bagi saya mungkin beliau merujuk desas-desus bahawa Umno Negeri Sembilan sebenarnya mahu Jalaluddin Alias sebagai menteri besar, dan bukannya Ismail. Jalaluddin ialah watak utama dalam gerakan tarik sokongan terhadap Aminuddin.
Puad juga dipetik berkata, perkembangan krisis Negeri Sembilan memalukan Umno kerana pengundi telah memberi mandat kuat untuk mendirikan sebuah kerajaan yang stabil.
Oleh itu saya terkejut apabila Presiden Umno Zahid Hamidi dipetik Malaysiakini 9 Sept lalu berkata, "sebaik mungkin kita tidak akan mengotorkan tangan untuk menyantuni situasi di Negeri Sembilan".

Saya ulangi gerakan yang akhirnya memaksa PRN diadakan dicetuskan Umno Negeri Sembilan. Tidak pasti sama ada Umno induk merestui tindakan itu tetapi Umno Negeri Sembilan sebahagian Umno. Masalah Umno Negeri Sembilan ialah masalah Umno induk juga.
Apa lagi dalam kalangan 14 Adun Umno Negeri Sembilan yang tarik sokongan terhadap Aminuddin dulu ialah Mohamad Hasan, timbalan Zahid sendiri. Gadang dalam parti.

Diakui Zahid ada mengadakan pertemuan dengan Ismail semasa Perhimpunan Agung Umno berlangsung tempoh hari. Pasti bincang mengenai krisis dan perkembangan di Negeri Sembilan. Tidak tahu apa hasilnya dan apa perancangannya.

Apa pun yang jelas ialah Umno induk, like it or not, kena 'kotorkan tangan' terutama setelah pelantikan exco dilucutkan tetapi tidak diterima menteri besar. Ia tidak boleh lepas tangan and walk away from Negeri Sembilan begitu sahaja.
Artikel ini ialah pandangan penulis dan tidak semestinya mewakili FMT.

e821244614f87904: LONDON: Charles Spencer's book about his late sister, Princess Diana, packed with explosive revelations, is published Tuesday, after searing extracts prompted a rare and sharp rebuttal from King Charles III.
Almost three decades after Diana was killed in a car crash in Paris in 1997, people remain fascinated by her life and tragic death.
"Swan Song: Diana, My Sister", a memoir written by Diana's younger brother, has been published by Penguin and translated into 12 languages.
But extracts serialised in the British tabloid the Daily Mail over the past few days have triggered sensational headlines.
Spencer has said he wrote the book to "speak on Diana's behalf" and correct "untruths that have become accepted over time".
"Diana would be cheering from the rafters at this book, I have no doubt about that," he told the Mail on Sunday at the weekend.
Published excerpts claimed her ex-husband, Charles, then Prince of Wales and now the king, told Spencer in a phone call shortly after Diana's death, "Rest assured, we'll forget her soon enough."
Her death, aged just 36, sparked an outpouring of grief in Britain for the woman dubbed "the people's princess".
And it triggered accusations that the then monarch, Queen Elizabeth II, failed to respond swiftly with empathy and understanding.
Spencer claimed Charles had "sounded giddily elated, like a lottery winner" at the news of Diana's demise.
And he said Charles "went ballistic" after he insisted Diana would not have wanted her sons, princes William and Harry, then aged 15 and 12, to walk behind her coffin in her funeral procession.

A Buckingham Palace spokesperson issued a rare reaction from the 77-year-old king, saying: "His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgement and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss."
'Gaslit by king'
"The king is plainly furious, Buckingham Palace almost never issues any statement like that," BBC journalist Laura Kuenssberg said during a Friday interview.
"Those are exactly the words he said," Spencer assured her, adding, "I don't hear (King Charles) saying he didn't say that."
Spencer criticised the palace's implication that his grief had affected his recollection, telling The Mail on Sunday: "It is not every day you wake up to find you've been gaslit by the king."
He also dubbed it a "rather poor imitation" of the palace's response to Prince Harry and his wife Meghan's claims of royal racism five years ago – which was that "recollections may vary".
Charles and Diana's tumultuous marriage between 1981 and 1996 was regularly featured in British newspapers.
And Spencer reveals Diana had at times contemplated suicide, driving down to Beachy Head, a notorious clifftop in southern England where people used to deliberately fall to their deaths.
But her love for her sons "stopped her from going further," he writes.
Spencer also recalled Diana told him she and Charles were divorcing because he was "in love with his valet", adding he did not ask why "she would believe such an improbable thing".
Charles later married his long-time mistress, Camilla Parker Bowles, who is now the queen.
'Vindictive'
But royal experts have questioned some of the book's claims.
Royal biographer Robert Hardman wrote on X that he witnessed Charles, rather than elated, "distraught and in tears" at Diana's funeral.
Andrew Morton, author of the 1992 book "Diana: Her True Story", in a comment in The Times, wrote that Spencer's claims about the phone call with Charles were "incendiary and disputed".
While royal commentator Jennie Bond told the BBC the memoir was a "vindictive account".
Spencer, 62, has worked as a US television journalist and calls himself a historian.
He inherited the Spencer family's stately home, Althorp, where he and Diana grew up. She is buried on an island in the grounds.
After her death, he accused the media of having "blood on their hands", and in his raw eulogy at Diana's funeral, he vowed to always look out for her two sons.
But he did not mention her beau Dodi Fayed, who was also killed in the Paris crash, even though in the memoir he praised the son of Harrods owner, Mohamed Al-Fayed, for being "kind to Diana".

But in a shocking claim, Spencer wrote Diana had felt "revulsion" for Mohamed Al-Fayed, who had squeezed her buttocks, and said, "In a leery, suggestive tone, 'And in Egypt, father-in-law gets first go.'"
Spencer also told the BBC the media's "cancerous influence" on Prince Harry and his wife, Meghan, recalled Diana's hounding by the British press.
45b53596b69267b0: PARIS, Sept 22 — Zinedine Zidane spent years patiently waiting in the wings for his chance to manage France and on Friday the successor to Didier Deschamps as coach of Les Bleus will lead the side out for the first time in a Uefa Nations League tie in Turkey.
Now 54, Zidane is widely recognised as one of the all-time great French players, alongside Michel Platini.

Deschamps was the captain of the first France team to win the World Cup, as hosts in 1998, and of the side that won Euro 2000. But Zidane was the inspiration in those sides, a majestic playmaker with balletic ball control as well as a wicked side to his game.
He bowed out of international football as a player 20 years ago with his infamous headbutt on Marco Materazzi in extra time of the World Cup final in Berlin which France lost on penalties to Italy.
That game was the 108th and last time that Zidane, the Marseille-born son of Algerian immigrants, played for France.
But he left his home country to move abroad aged just 24, when he quit Bordeaux for Juventus.

Zidane never returned, spending five years in Italy before the finest days of his playing career came at Real Madrid. He then enjoyed two separate spells coaching the Spanish giants, winning the Champions League three years running between 2016 and 2018.
His second stint in charge at the Bernabeu ended in 2021, and ever since he has simply been biding his time, preparing for the call to come.

“I have been waiting four or five years for this day. I am filled with emotion, I am really excited. I am happy. This is huge for me,” Zidane said at his unveiling in Paris in late July, as a new era started for France following the 14-year reign of Deschamps.
“Welcome home,” Kylian Mbappe posted on Instagram upon Zidane’s appointment.
Attacking promise

On Friday he announced his first squad, and there were several new faces amid expectations that his team will be more attack-minded than France were for the majority of the Deschamps era, at least up until the recent World Cup.

“You will get to see how I see football. Playing good football is what gets me going. There will always be a balance to the side, but I want to see us play and I think we have the team to do that,” he said.

After years of favouring substance over style, leading to some criticism but also a World Cup triumph in 2018, Deschamps realised he had the players to play more on the front foot at this year’s tournament in North America.

France were the favourites only to end up losing to Spain in the semi-finals, but captain Mbappe was the tournament’s top scorer with 10 goals while Michael Olise was outstanding. Last year’s Ballon d’Or Ousmane Dembele shone intermittently.

That trio are all present in Zidane’s squad, with the new coach confirming Mbappe as captain. Injured Arsenal defender William Saliba and Aurelien Tchouameni of Real Madrid are notable absentees, while there are several new faces.

Centre-back Jeremy Jacquet was called up as a reward for an impressive start to the season at Liverpool, while midfielder Lucas Da Cunha of Como is an intriguing addition and Esteban Lepaul of Rennes deserved his chance after top-scoring in Ligue 1 last season.
Zidane’s assistant will be David Bettoni, who worked with him at Real. Fabien Barthez, who won the World Cup with Zidane, will be the goalkeeping coach.
The first major objective for the new manager will be Euro 2028 in the UK and Ireland, before the World Cup in Morocco, Spain and Portugal in 2030.
Deschamps has set the bar high in terms of expectations, with France getting to at least the semi-finals in five of the last six major tournaments.
First up, though, is the Nations League, which gives Zidane some tough tests to begin but without the pressure of the Euros or World Cup.
Les Bleus face Turkey and Belgium away before Zidane makes his home bow at the Stade de France on October 2 against Italy, an occasion that will stir memories of Materazzi and 2006. — AFP
94319244ffad2b03: KOTA BHARU, Sept 22 — Kelantan recorded losses of RM33.47 million in commercial crime from January to August this year, an increase of RM5.97 million compared with RM27.50 million reported during the same period last year.
Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the number of commercial crime cases also rose from 1,100 to 1,921, an increase of 821 cases.
He said one of the most significant increases was in e-commerce scams, which rose from 260 to 657 cases, while other cybercrimes also increased from 287 to 444 cases.

“This trend shows that crime is increasingly changing in line with technological developments. Therefore, our actions must also change rapidly, particularly in prevention and public awareness,” he said in his speech at the monthly assembly at the Kelantan contingent police headquarters here yesterday.

However, Mohd Yusoff said the overall crime index for the Kelantan contingent from January to August this year fell three per cent to 1,213 cases compared with 1,251 cases during the same period in 2025.
He said violent crime also declined 11 per cent from 310 to 276 cases, while property crime fell from 941 to 937 cases.
On the drug threat, he said narcotics cases decreased 13 per cent from 18,427 to 16,044 during the period, while arrests fell 10 per cent from 19,469 to 17,579.
He said the value of drugs seized also declined 31.49 per cent from RM25.47 million to RM17.45 million, as a result of more systematic and focused efforts to combat the threat.

In terms of prevention, Mohd Yusoff said the state police continued to implement various approaches, including MPV and URB patrols, AMANITA, community policing programmes and networks with relevant agencies.

He said community participation through the Volunteer Smartphone Patrol (VSP) also needed to be further strengthened, with 150,019 people having registered as VSP members in the Kelantan contingent as of Aug 31.

He said efforts to engage with young people should also take into account the influence of screens, social media and the digital world, which increasingly shape their lives, while maintaining face-to-face interaction to build public trust.
Mohd Yusoff said these ongoing efforts were important to ensure that public safety was always safeguarded, in line with the police’s responsibility to maintain peace in the state. — Bernama
d27eaf4f9609211a: SAO PAULO, Sept 22 — Brazilian Joao Fonseca announced on Monday that he would “skip the Asian swing” in order to recover physically and mentally after a season of injury lows and on-court highs.

The 20-year-old, one of the most promising young talents on the ATP tour, wrote on Instagram: “2026 has been a very challenging year for me. On top of everything the profession demands, a series of injuries ended up taking me out of important tournaments and keeping me from playing the way I would like to.
“I talked a lot with my team, and we came to the conclusion that the best decision right now is to listen to my body, give my mind and body a break, and skip the Asian swing.”
After missing the US Open due to abdominal pain, Fonseca made his comeback last weekend during Brazil’s 3-1 victory over Switzerland in the Davis Cup.
He beat Dominic Stricker 4-6, 6-3, 6-2 to get his country off to a winning start in Rio de Janeiro.
“I made a huge effort to return and represent Brazil in the Davis Cup, but I still need more time,” the world number 28 added.
“I know that’s just part of an athlete’s life, but even so, it’s still frustrating.”
Fonseca will miss the ATP 500 event in Tokyo, which will run from September 30–October 6, and the Shanghai Masters over the following fortnight.
Earlier this year, the South American suffered recurring back problems which led to his elimination in the first round of the Australian Open.

Despite these issues, Fonseca has had some standout moments this season, such as his victory over Novak Djokovic in the third round of the French Open on his way to a debut quarter-final appearance at a Grand Slam. He also reached the third round at Wimbledon. — AFP
3d122e00ae7ea4d3: NAGOYA, Sept 22 — The mission to defend the gold medal at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games is not merely about repeating the success for national women’s squash player S. Sivasangari, but is also an important platform in her bid to qualify for the Olympic Games.

The 27-year-old player admitted that this factor provided additional motivation ahead of the women’s singles competition, which begins tomorrow, but at the same time acknowledged that it also brought pressure to achieve the desired target.
“Of course, the goal is to win gold and defend the title, but everyone wants to win. That is not the question.
“The question is how I will prepare for each match and how I want to be mentally prepared,” she told Bernama when met at the Nagoya Kinjofuto Arena here.

Sivasangari said representing Malaysia was always something special to her, while the opportunity to pursue an Olympic berth through winning gold was another motivation for her to give her best in Aichi-Nagoya.
“Both are important. Representing Malaysia is always a big thing, and the Asian Games are also very important to me.
“This year, there is another motivation, which is to secure an Olympic berth. So, it is an additional motivation and additional pressure,” she said.
However, she did not want to think too much about the ultimate target, choosing instead to focus on each match that she has to play.

She said the mental aspect would play a major role after undergoing physical preparations through about one and a half months of intensive training in Prague, Czech Republic, before beginning her Professional Squash Association (PSA) season by competing in London and Qatar.
“I have done the work physically, but when I arrive at the tournament, it is more about the mental aspect.
“I want to win; that is the goal, but in the process there are many other things that I need to focus on. I just want to take it one step at a time and focus on what I need to do,” she said.
Sivasangari said the two PSA tournaments had also helped her regain her competitive rhythm after undergoing a lengthy training period.
“I think I played better in Qatar. Of course, the more matches you play, the better your rhythm becomes.

“I am happy to be here and excited to compete in my third Asian Games. I have just found my rhythm after playing in two consecutive tournaments, and I am still fresh, still want to fight and still want to play,” she said.
Sivasangari previously made history by winning gold in the women’s singles and women’s team events at the Hangzhou 2022 Asian Games and is now in Aichi-Nagoya aiming to defend the titles. — Bernama
06c4970cc1f3a4f2: NEW YORK, Sept 22 — The United Kingdom has signed on to an initiative urging UN Security Council permanent members to withhold their vetoes on matters concerning mass atrocities, such as genocide, countries leading the push said Monday.

The initiative, first proposed by Mexico and France in 2015, now has a total of 128 countries behind it, French foreign minister Jean-Noel Barrot and Mexican counterpart Roberto Velasco said in a joint statement.
It is now just one country shy of reaching a two-thirds threshold of UN member states.
The Security Council has been paralyzed on many issues in recent years amid deep divisions between the five veto-wielding permanent members: France, UK, Russia, China, and the United States.

“By supporting this political declaration, states are demonstrating their commitment to ensuring that the Security Council can fully exercise its primary responsibility for maintaining international peace and security,” said Barrot and Velasco.
In May, a diplomatic source told AFP that France was hoping to reach the two-thirds majority before this year’s UN General Assembly, which kicks off this week.
Even if adopted with a two-thirds majority, the resolution would be non-binding.
Officials nonetheless hope to make it more politically difficult for a permanent member to use its veto in cases of such dire emergencies. — AFP

Itu sahaja sudah cukup membuatkan saya mahu tahu apa yang akan dibuatnya apabila sebuah panggung diserahkan kepada beliau.

Ternyata saya tidak kecewa. Mansur & Liu elok pembikinannya. Penataan cahaya, permainan bayang-bayang, skrin LED yang dimanfaatkan sepenuhnya, kesan khas, kostum, pergerakan pelakon (blocking) dan keseluruhannya membuatkan kita tak sangka bahawa apa yang sedang kita lihat sebenarnya berlaku di atas sebuah pentas. Malah, keasyikan menonton membuat saya terlupa di bangku sebelah saya, duduk seorang kawan yang sudah lama saya tak jumpa dan di belakang pula seorang seniman sohor bersama isterinya. Saya ralit melayan lagu, muzik dan bunyian mengiringi pertuturan dan gerak lakon.

M Nasir mencipta kira-kira 30 lagu dan skor untuk pementasan ini. Itu memang kekuatan beliau. Dengan sistem bunyi Panggung Sari yang berkesan, ada ketikanya kita terasa bunyi itu datang dari seluruh ruang atau seakan terhasil dari dalam gegendang telinga kita sendiri.

Bahan asas Mansur & Liu sebenarnya sudah ada dalam Sulalatus Salatin. Dalam naskhah lama itu diceritakan hubungan Melaka dengan China di zaman Sultan Mansur Syah pada abad ke-15. Kisah Maharaja China ditimpa kedal (sejenis penyakit kulit) yang tidak mampu disembuhkan oleh beratus-ratus tabib. Seorang tabib tua akhirnya memberitahu bahawa penawarnya ialah air basuhan kaki Sultan Mansur Syah. Air itu diminta dari Melaka, dibawa ke China oleh Tun Perpatih Putih, lalu diminum dan digunakan untuk membasuh tubuh baginda. Sembuhlah Raja China.

Naskhah asal Mansur & Liu ditulis oleh Allahyarham Zakaria Ariffin sebelum dikembangkan dan diolah semula oleh pasukan penulis untuk pementasan ini. Di tangan M Nasir, ruang antara sejarah dan hikayat itu dikembangkan menjadi sebuah fiksyen 'ada cerita di sebalik cerita'. Dalam versi teater ini, Maharaja (lakonan Anas Ridzuan) yang gembira kerana berjaya disembuhkan telah menghantar puterinya, Liu untuk dijodohkan dengan Sultan Mansur (lakonan Aliff Aziz). Dahulu memang begitu. Perkahwinan adalah satu kaedah mengeratkan hubungan diplomatik antara dua kerajaan atau empayar. Bermakna, perkahwinan juga adalah kerja politik.

Liu (lakonan Melinda Dadew) kecewa kerana dia sudah mempunyai kekasih bernama Lin Hao, laksamana China (lakonan Brian Chan). Lin Hao, seperti juga Liu, patah hati apatah lagi dia sendiri harus mengetuai pelayaran membawa kekasih yang dicintainya menyeberangi laut untuk diserahkan kepada orang lain. Tetapi dia seorang laksamana. Dia harus memilih untuk taat setia kepada maharaja dan negaranya. Dia seperti Hang Tuah membawa Tun Teja kepada Sultan Mahmud Syah yang mana dalam beberapa versi, ada permainan perasaan antara Tuah dan Tun Teja. Taat kepada raja mengatasi segala-galanya.

Elemen 'spin-off' ini pastinya akan membuat kita lebih terasa seolah turut berada pada zaman itu dan mudah untuk kita menjiwainya. Inilah kekuatan karya kreatif dalam membawa apa juga mesej termasuklah propaganda. Tidaklah terasa macam menonton cerita yang diambil bulat-bulat dari buku teks Sejarah sekolah.

Teater Mansur & Liu yang dipentaskan selama 10 hari, bermula 10 Sept hingga 20 Sept itu adalah kisah cinta romantik yang disulam dengan elemen perebutan kuasa, peperangan dan sudah pastilah pengkhianatan - satu penyakit yang akan tetap berlaku selagi adanya manusia. Barang harus diingat, pengkhianatan itu bermaksud ia selalunya datang dari dalam.

Dalam sejarah, banyak kerajaan tumbang kerana pengkhianatan atau persengketaan sesama sendiri, bukan musuh dari luar. Granada, kerajaan Islam terakhir di Semenanjung Iberia, misalnya, bukan sahaja berdepan serangan tentera Kristian Sepanyol, tetapi pada masa yang sama berdepan perebutan kuasa dalam keluarga pemerintah sendiri. Perpecahan dalaman itu melemahkan Granada ketika musuh sedang menyerang dari luar. Akhirnya Granada jatuh pada 1492. Tetapi, eh buat apa tengok jauh-jauh? Hari ini apa kurangnya? Depan mata kita pun sedang berlaku juga persengketaan dan perang saudara sedemikian rupa, kan?

Dalam Mansur & Liu, 'barua' itu ialah Datuk Syahbandar lakonan Amerul Affendi yang memang cukup membuat kita menyampah. Dia berada dalam lingkungan kekuasaan Melaka tetapi mempunyai permainannya sendiri. Dia berpakat dengan pemimpin Siam, Somdet Phra (lakonan Hazama) untuk menggugat Melaka. Datuk Syahbandar juga menggunakan keluarga Mansur sendiri iaitu Tun Seri Anom (lakonan Arena Wan), sepupu yang menaruh hati terhadap Mansur tetapi dianggap Mansur seperti adiknya sendiri. Anom bersama ibunya, Tun Ratna Kenchana (lakonan Ruzana Ibrahim) membubuh racun dalam minuman Liu tetapi rancangan tersebut gagal dan dari situlah rahsia segala pengkhianatan terbongkar. Orang 'China' yang dicurigai kononnya musuh dari luar rupanya adalah kawan yang setia manakala saudara sendirilah sebenarnya gunting dalam lipatan.

Saya pernah menulis sebelum ini tentang pemerhatian saya ketika berada di Pulau Singkep, Kepulauan Riau, Indonesia. Di sana saya melihat bagaimana Melayu dan Cina boleh hidup bersama dengan begitu biasa. Mereka berniaga, berjiran, bergaul dan menjalani kehidupan. 'Chemistry' perpaduan ini jika dipupuk sihat mampu menjadikan kita negara kuat dan gagah di rantau ini.

Mansur & Liu membawa semangat yang begitu. Malah dalam Sulalatus Salatin, selepas Raja China sembuh, baginda dikisahkan berpesan kepada keturunannya supaya hendaklah China dan Melaka hidup dalam 'muafakat berkasih-kasihan jua'. Hubungan erat Melaka dengan China dalam Mansur & Liu digambarkan sebagai kerjasama dua tamadun yang tidak mengurangkan salah satu kerajaan pun tetapi menjadikan kedua empayar ini makin kukuh.

Apa pun, formula perpaduan ini di atas kertas memanglah senang tetapi manusia tetap manusia. Pasti ada kejahatan di sana-sini kerana memburu kepentingan peribadi. Perang pun berlaku demi untuk menentukan siapa yang lebih berhak berkuasa.

Bagi saya kalau Mansur & Liu hendak diadaptasikan ke layar filem dengan skala seperti yang saya tonton malam itu, memang makan modal besar. Filem epik bukan kerja murah. Kapal, istana, peperangan, tentera, kostum, empayar China dan Melaka serta Siam. Fuh! Belum apa-apa produser sudah demam. Maka, teater mampu menjadi sebuah tempat yang tepat untuk imaginasi sebesar ini direalisasikan. Teater mempunyai satu kelebihan yang filem tidak ada. Ia tidak perlu menunjukkan semuanya secara nyata.

Cahaya, bayang-bayang, kesan visual dan bunyi mampu menjadi laut, kapal, istana malah juga bala tentera. Penonton akan terpukau kagum dengan kecanggihan teknikal ini. Di layar filem, jika silap guna kesan khas, boleh ditertawakan. Untuk sebuah debut pengarahan teater, M Nasir mengambil risiko besar dan pada saya, beliau berjaya.

Selepas pementasan selesai, saya sempat bertemu beberapa kawan yang terlibat seperti Amerul Affendi, Taqim Zaki (pemeran watak Tun Perpatih Putih), Hazama dan Anas Ridzuan. Saya peluk mereka seorang demi seorang dengan bangga. Apabila bertemu M Nasir, saya peluk juga beliau kerana tumpang bangga. M Nasir macam biasalah, ketawa mengekek.

Oleh kerana teater Mansur & Liu versi M Nasir ini memilih untuk bermain fiksyen di sebalik sejarah, saya sebagai penonton pun berhaklah bermain di ruang yang sama. Sebab itu ada perkara yang buat saya geram. Saya memang mempunyai masalah dengan cerita cinta yang berakhir bahagia. Barangkali Mansur & Liu bagi saya ialah Zainuddin dan Hayati dalam Tenggelamnya Kapal Van der Wijck karya Hamka tetapi yang ini versi M Nasir. Atau mungkin juga Mansur & Liu adalah Jack dan Rose dalam filem Titanic. Bezanya Zainuddin dan Hayati tidak diberikan kesempatan untuk hidup bahagia. Jack pula tenggelam bersama Titanic dan meninggalkan Rose meneruskan hidup dengan sebuah kenangan. Saya suka begitu. Saya mahu diseksa.

Alang-alang berfantasikan sebuah kisah cinta besar, biarlah akhirnya saya keluar dari panggung dengan dada sesak. Biarlah salah seorang mati, hilang atau mereka tidak dapat bersama selama-lamanya. Cinta yang tidak kesampaian selalunya dianggap sebuah cinta yang paling agung.

Tetapi Mansur & Liu bukan untuk membuat kita bersedih. Ia mahu kita menghargai cinta dan keamanan. Ia mahu melihat kita mengenepikan perbezaan dan mencari persamaan untuk sebuah penyatuan. Ia mahu kita hapuskan persengketaan, bangkit semula setelah jatuh dan berbahagia setelah sembuh daripada luka.
Atas sebab itulah sewaktu memandu pulang, telinga saya masih terngiang-ngiang bait nyanyian Maharaja China apabila baginda sembuh daripada sakitnya:
“Be-ta dah sem-buh!” Kemudian disambut suara nyanyian beramai-ramai:
“Ra-ja dah sem-buh!" Chenggg! "Ra-ja dah sem-buh!"

Dengan bunyi gaya opera Cina, ia kedengaran lucu sehingga menimbulkan ketawa penonton tetapi jelas bait tersebut cukup menangkap telinga dan sangat berkesan masuk ke jiwa sehingga kita boleh menyanyikannya di rumah. Rupanya saya juga telah disembuhkan.
"Aku dah sembuh! Aku dah sembuh!" nyanyi saya sehingga ke saat ini.
Malam itu saya puas. Luka saya pun turut sembuh.

679601fdd0565d10: JAKARTA, Sept 22 — Indonesia’s Press Council has described the five journalists who went missing while covering the Anak Krakatau eruption at the Sunda Straits, as “heroes of the press”, highlighting the risks journalists face when reporting from hazardous areas.

Its chairman Komarudin Hidayat said the five had sought to bring the best images to the public, while the incident should serve as a reminder for media organisations to coordinate closely with local authorities when assigning journalists to dangerous areas.

“We usually enjoy the images but sometimes forget the struggle behind obtaining them. When a tragedy like this happens, we are reminded just how costly and difficult it can be to get the best images,” he said after a prayer gathering for the missing journalists in Jakarta on Monday, according to Antara News Agency.

The missing journalists are Muhammad Bagus Khoirunnas of Antara, Firdaus Wajidi of Anadolu Agency, Ari Basuki of Merdeka.com, Yudistiro Pranoto of iNews and freelance journalist Donal Husni. They were travelling with boat crew members Warta and Surakman, and guide Heriyanto.
All eight have been missing since September 7 after their speedboat lost contact while they were on a reporting assignment in the Sunda Strait.
The joint search and rescue operation was officially called off on September 17 after 10 days without finding any trace of them.

In his remarks at the gathering, which was streamed live, Komarudin reflected on the value of human life and the uncertainty faced by the families of those missing, while repeatedly expressing hope for their return.
“We pray that they return. We still need them, and at this stage of life, we still want them to continue,” he said.

As the media community continues to remember the missing journalists, Antara has dedicated a room at its Banten bureau to photojournalist Muhammad Bagus, who had worked with the national news agency in the province for eight years, in recognition of his dedication and journalistic work.

Antara Director of News Virgandhi Prayudantoro said the room, which will bear Bagus’ name, would preserve his photojournalistic works while serving as an educational and creative space for Antara journalists and other media practitioners in Banten. — Bernama
90e926da3e6797e8: SINGAPORE, Sept 22 — At least S$4.8 million (RM15.3 million) has been lost in Singapore since January to scams involving fraudsters impersonating Harvey Norman employees, police said.
The police said on Monday that 119 cases had been reported this year, with victims targeted through unsolicited calls, according to CNA.

The scammers typically claim that the victims had purchased a television or had a delivery pending, before telling those who denied making the purchase that their personal information had been misused.
Victims are then connected to another scammer posing as an officer from the Monetary Authority of Singapore, who alleges that they are linked to offences such as money laundering.
Under the guise of assisting with an investigation, the victims are instructed to move their money into a so-called safe account.
Some are instead told to withdraw cash, purchase gold bars or hand over valuables including jewellery and luxury watches to people claiming to be involved in the investigation.
The scammers assure victims that their money and belongings will be returned once the purported investigation is completed.
Victims later realise they have been deceived after making multiple transfers without receiving the promised refunds.

Police reminded the public that Singapore government officials will never instruct anyone to transfer or surrender cash or valuables, provide banking login credentials, install mobile applications from unverified app stores, or transfer calls to police or other government agencies.
Members of the public can use the ScamShield app to help guard against scam calls and SMSes, while those unsure about a suspected scam can contact the 24-hour ScamShield helpline at 1799.
de128c74977006d1: SEPTEMBER 22 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said yesterday that the state's executive councillors (excos) remain in office, arguing that the Yang di-Pertuan Besar cannot remove them without his advice.

In a statement a day after the palace announced it had revoked the appointments of all excos, Ismail said the state's administrative system rests on constitutional monarchy and parliamentary democracy.

“Based on Part Two of the UUTKNS 1959, the sovereign power of the Ruler in matters of state administration shall be exercised on the advice of the YAB Menteri Besar and the State Executive Council,” he said, citing Article 40(1) of the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan (UUTKNS).

There are seven Chapters in Part Two of the UUTKNS 1959. Chapter 2 is on the Executive. The Chapter has 11 Articles — that is, Articles 35 to 44, including Article 39A which was amended into the UUTKNS in 1965.
Article 40 is rightly cited by Ismail as providing for the Ruler to act on advice.

But let’s not forget Article 37 on Appointment of State Secretary, Legal Adviser and Financial Officer. Clause (1) says there shall be constituted the offices of State Secretary, State Legal Adviser and State Financial Officer; and the appointments thereto shall be made by the appropriate Service Commission from amongst members of any of the relevant public services.
Clause (2)(b) says the State Legal Adviser shall advise on legal matters referred to him by the Yang di-Pertuan Besar or the State Government.

Under Clause (3), the State Secretary, Legal Adviser and Financial Officer official shall have the right to take part in the proceedings of the State Executive Council and the Legislative Assembly and may be appointed to any Committee thereof but shall not have any vote in the State Executive Council or the Legislative Assembly or in any such Committee.

The State Legal Adviser must have rendered his legal advice to the Yang di-Pertuan Besar in respect of the latter’s revocation of the appointments of the excos with immediate effect for breaching their oath of office through their actions and statements on September 15.

Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir (centre) receives a memorandum from non-governmental organisations, presented by Prof Dr Mohd Aluwi Sari, after Friday prayers at the Tuanku Munawir Royal Mosque in Seri Menanti on September 18, 2026. The Negeri Sembilan Ruler’s powers and the role of the Menteri Besar are at the centre of a constitutional dispute over the state executive council. — Bernama pic
The same legal adviser should be advising the State Government headed by Ismail on the legal matter.
So, it is curious that Ismail should say that the Yang di-Pertuan Besar “cannot remove [the excos] without his advice”.
